करमचंद गांधी उपरोक्त सभी राज्यों के दीवा: Karamchand Gandhi was the Diwan of all above States. He was the father of Gandhiji. He is better known as Kaba Gandhi.
1894 में गांधीजी ने दक्षिण अफ्रीका में ': In 1894 Gandhiji founded ‘ Natal Indian Congress’ in South Africa and during this long Movement in South Africa he got imprisonment several times. He founded the ‘Tolstoy Farm’ with his associates and started living there. He published a newspaper “Indian Opinion” in South Africa and founded “ Phoenix Farm” in 1904 in Durban.
गांधीजी के विचार में जोर आदर्शवाद पर नही: In Gandhiji’s thought the emphasis is not on idealism, but on practical idealism, Gandhi’s thought has also been linked to Utopian socialism and Philosophical Anarchism and can be compared with strands of Marxist (though not a western philosophy) and even western liberal thought. He believed that in the concept of ideal non-violent state, every citizen would have the feeling of self-governance and in this stage, there would be no need for the state to comply with the law of the land.
सत्य और अहिंसा महात्मा गांधी के राम राज्: Truth and non-violence are twin principles of Mahatma Gandhi’s Ram Rajya. He used truth and non-violence as the base to develop a new society of his dream. Some people believe that the policy of truth of Mahatma Gandhi is inspired by Hindu religion and non-violence from Buddha, Jain, and Christian ideology.
गांधी के दर्शन के अनुसार 'सत्य' का अर्थ: According to Gandhi’s philosophy ‘Truth’ stands for ‘reality.’ He described Truth as existence, consciousness and Bliss. He said ‘Ahimsa’ or ‘Non-violence’ is the means; Truth is the end. They are so intertwined that it is impossible to separate them.
गांधी के विचार को दार्शनिक अराजकतावाद से: Gandhi’s thought has been linked to philosophical anarchism and can be compared with strands of Marxist thought. But during present circumstances, he was not in the favour to abolish the state. Human being are not capable enough to manage their collective affairs on their own. Hence, State and law are required in the society. In addition to this, he also believed that the jurisdiction of the State should be minimum. Gandhi told Louis Fischer "I am a true socialist. The meaning of my socialism is Sarvodaya." There is a great similarity between Gandhi and Marx, the ﬁ nal aim of both of them was to establish a stateless and classless society, but their means of achieving this aim was different. For Gandhi, it was through non-violence, but for Marx, it was through violent means.
हड़ताल, सत्याग्रह की गांधीवादी रणनीति का: The strike was the last step in Gandhian strategy of Satyagraha while fasting was the ﬁ rst step in Gandhian strategy of Satyagraha. He termed fasting as ‘Fire Arrow.’
गांधी के सत्याग्रह का अर्थ अहिंसा है, जो: Gandhi’s Satyagraha means non-violence, as a force greater than violence. Suffering was its driving force, once let the oppressors use as much force as they can on the non-violent protesters until a stage come when they can incur no more violence. Hence there is no motive to defeat the enemy but to change their perception.
गांधीजी के अनुसार, हिंसा का सबसे क्रूर र: According to Gandhiji, the cruellest form of violence is the persistence of poverty.
गांधीजी ने परिवार नियोजन के लिए 'आत्म-नि: Gandhiji told ‘Self- Control’ as the best mean for family planning.
गांधीजी दक्षिण अफ्रीका में लगभग 21 वर्ष: Gandhiji lived approx 21 years in South Africa. In 1893 at the age of 24, he went to South Africa to appear in a case of Gujarati businessman Dada Abdulla. He returned to India in January, 1915.
जनवरी, 1915 में महात्मा गांधी दक्षिण अफ्: In January, 1915 Mahatma Gandhi returned from South Africa and people warmly welcomed him. The struggles and success in South Africa made him very popular in India. In India, he came in contact with Gopal Krishna Gokhale and accepted him as his political mentor. He linked himself to India’s active politics under the inﬂ uence of Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
व्यवसायी दादा अब्दुल्ला के कानूनी सलाहका: Gandhi arrived in Durban, South Africa in 1893 to serve as legal counsel to the businessman Dada Abdulla. In June, he was asked by Dada Abdulla to undertake a trip to Pretoria in the Transvaal, a journey which ﬁ rst took Gandhi to Pietermaritzburg. There Gandhi was seated in the ﬁ rst-class compartment since he had purchased a ﬁ rst-class ticket. A European who entered the compartment hastened to summon railway ofﬁ cials, who ordered Gandhi to shift himself to the van compartment since ‘coolies’ and non-whites were apparently not permitted in ﬁ rst-class compartments. Gandhi protested and produced his ticket, but was warned that he would be forcibly removed if he did not make a gracious exit. As Gandhi refused to comply with the order, he was summarily pushed out of the train, and his luggage was tossed out on to the platform.
महात्मा गांधी ने पहली बार वर्ष 1901 में: Mahatma Gandhi attended the Calcutta session of Indian National Congress in the year 1901 for the ﬁ rst time.
गांधीजी का सत्याग्रह आश्रम मूल रूप से एक: Gandhi’s Satyagraha Ashram was originally established at the Kocharab Bungalow of Jivanlal Desai, a barrister, and friend of Gandhi. At that time, the Ashram was called the Satyagraha Ashram. But Gandhi wanted to carry out various activities such as farming and animal husbandry, in addition to other pursuits which required a much larger area of usable land. So two years later, on 17 June 1917, the Ashram was relocated to an area of thirty-six acres on the banks of the River Sabarmati, in Ahmedabad and later came to be known as the Sabarmati Ashram.
गांधीजी ने फीनिक्स स्टेशन के पास कुछ जमी: Gandhi purchased some land near Phoenix station and established the Phoenix Ashram in 1904. It was reopened on 27 February, 2000. It was the ﬁ rst Ashram established by Gandhiji.
दक्षिण अफ्रीका में अपने प्रवास के दौरान,: During his stay in South Africa, Mahatma Gandhi rendered his services as an attendant to the helpless poor patients in the charity hospitals of Rustumji. Here, he gave his voluntary services as a compounder. He also served there the wounded soldiers of the Boer War.
दक्षिण अफ्रीका में ही गांधीजी ने स्वयं क: It was in South Africa that Gandhiji discovered himself. He emerged from shy and timid youth as a successful organiser and leader. It was only after the struggles of Sotuh Africa that he prepared himself for the leadership of Indian national movement. Militancy is generally associated with violent methods of struggles. But Gandhiji's struggle in South Africa was completely non-violent and based on Satyagraha. Hence Reason (R) can not be considered right.
गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले भारत में ब्रिटिश साम्र: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was one of the early social and political leaders during the Indian Independence Movement against the British Empire in India. Gokhale was famously a mentor of Mahatma Gandhi in his formative years. In 1912, Gokhale visited South Africa at Gandhi’s invitation. As a young barrister, Gandhi returned from his struggles against the Empire in South Africa and received personal guidance from Gokhale, including knowledge and understanding of India and the issues confronting common Indians. By 1920, Gandhi emerged as the leader of the Indian Independence Movement. In his autobiography, Gandhi calls Gokhale as his mentor and guide.
गांधी जी के लिए राजनीति का मतलब समाज कल्: For Gandhi, politics meant social welfare and public welfare. The most important suggestion about politics from Gandhiji was ‘decentralization of power’. For him, the decentralization meant to encourage the village Panchayats and control their local administration.
गांधीजी ने राजनीति का जो प्रतिमान प्रस्त: The paradigm of politics presented by Gandhiji is the combination of three elements – morality, religion and humanity. But in Gandhian political model, there is no place for authority. He wanted to establish a Stateless Society.
बटक मियां बिहार में नील बागान के एक ब्रि: Batak Mian was a cook for a British manager of an Indigo plantation in Bihar known as Erwin in popular memory. During champaran Satyagrah he invited Gandhiji for dinner and coerced Batak Mian to poison Gandhi through milk. But Batak Mian while serving milk to Gandhiji, broke down and told Gandhiji about the poison and Gandhiji escaped unhurt. This story was corborated by Dr. Rajendra Prasad in one of his speech given in 1950s at Motihari which is mentioned in Delhi University Professor Dr. Girish Mishra's article "Gandhi's Champaran Struggle".
महात्मा गांधी के भतीजे मगन लाल गांधी ने: The nephew of Mahatma Gandhi, Magan Lal Gandhi ﬁ rst used the term ‘Sada Graha’ during a competition for which he was rewarded. Satyagraha means truth and rigidity. Later on, Gandhi improvised the word as ‘Satyagraha.’ Hence, it is clear that the word ‘Satyagraha’ was used ﬁ rstly by Gandhi.
सत्याग्रह दो शब्दों से मिलकर बना एक शब्द: Satyagraha is a term comprising two words; Satya or truth, and Agrah or insistence. Hence, in its loose English interpretation, Satyagraha means 'insistence on truth'. The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was Mahatma Gandhi’s ﬁ rst successful Satyagraha in India.
चंपारण सत्याग्रह के दौरान नील की खेती को: During the Champaran Satyagrah, the cultivation of Indigo was kwown as Tinkathia system. Tinkathia was the most prevalent system in Champaran. According to it, the factory owners convinced the tenant to grow indigo in a speciﬁ c area of his holding for which a ﬁ xed price was paid. In this, the ryot was under an obligation to cultivate three kathas per beegha of his land with indigo i.e. 3/20th of his land holding.
दक्षिण अफ्रीका में गांधी जी द्वारा किये: Struggle done by Gandhi in South Africa was termed as ‘Inactive resistance ‘but later Gandhi chose the word ‘Satyagraha’ in place of inactive resistance. Satyagraha was the term, which was used most during the freedom struggle. But Gandhi differentiated between Satyagraha and inactive resistance. As per him, inactive resistance is a political tool, whereas Satyagraha is moral power. He differentiated Inactive Resistance and Satyagraha by comparing it with the north and the south pole.
महात्मा गांधी ने विदेशी कपड़ों से निपटने: Mahatma Gandhi told destruction is the best method of dealing with foreign clothes. Gandhi related this destruction with the self-respect of Nation.
गांधीजी द्वारा ब्रिटिश निर्मित उत्पादों: Gandhi’s boycott of British made products was effective as British considered India as a major market for manufactured goods. A boycott of British goods leads to advance the market of Indian made goods like crafts and homemade items.
महात्मा गांधी के राजनीतिक जीवन का कालानु: The chronological sequence of the political life of Mahatma Gandhi is as follows : Event - Year Champaran Satyagraha - 1917 Ahmedabad Mill strike - February-March,1918 Kheda Satyagraha - March-June,1918 Non-cooperation movement - 1920-1922
अहमदाबाद मिल हड़ताल (1918) के दौरान, गां: During Ahmedabad mill strike (1918), Gandhiji used hunger strike as a weapon for ﬁ rst time.
उपरोक्त सभी घटनाएँ महात्मा गांधी से संबं: All of the above events are related to Mahatma Gandhi, held after his return to India (1915). Champaran Satyagraha was against forced Indigo farming in 1917, Ahmedabad Mill strike due to issue of Plague bonus, Kheda Satyagraha was against the payment of high taxes levied by the British, that people were unable to pay due to crop failure and plague epidemic. Satyagraha against Rowlatt Act which was passed to curb the revolutionary activities in India was launched in 1919 by Mahatma Gandhi. Chronologically option (a) is correct.
1917 का चंपारण सत्याग्रह भारत में महात्म: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was the ﬁ rst Satyagraha Mahatma Gandhi in India.

Naturally, the development of the country depends on the development of villages. That is why Gandhi stressed on the growth of rural industries such as khadi, handlooms, sericulture, handicrafts, etc. Rural industries are based on family labour and require less amount of capital. Raw materials are available in local and surrounding areas and the goods thus produced is sold in local markets. Therefore, there is no problem with production and market. Gandhi has strongly advocated the development of cottage industries in villages, which will reduce the burden on agriculture. Cottage industry can also work as a good support system for villagers. एका आंदोलन का जमीनी नेतृत्व मदारी पासी औ: The grassroot leadership of the Eka Movement was Madari Pasi and other low-caste leaders and many small Zamindars. Towards the end of 1921, peasant discontent resurfaced in some northern districts of the United Provinces—Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur etc. The issues involved were: (i) High rents—50 per cent higher than the recorded rates; (ii) Oppression by Thikedars in charge of revenue collection; and (iii) The practice of share-rents. The meetings of the Eka or the Unity Movement involved a symbolic religious ritual in which the assembled peasants vowed that they would: i. Pay only the recorded rent but would pay it on time; ii. Not leave when evicted; iii. Refuse to do forced labour; iv. No help to the criminals; v. Abide by Panchayat decisions. By March 1922, however, severe repression on the part of the authorities succeeded in bringing the Eka Movement to its end.

The act strengthened police powers so much that anybody could be arrested without any trial against them. In response Gandhji started Rowlatt Satyagrah (1919) which was although restricted to cities but turned to be the ﬁ rst all-India struggle against the British government.

The scope of the area was also very limited. But Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919) against the censure of freedom of press and detention without trial was proactively joined by all the sections of the society. Sentiments of the aggrieved common people were addressed. Knitting of people from all religions, all castes, all age groups, and both the genders in the Nationalist Movement had a distinguished characteristic of the Rowlatt Satyagraha. National newspapers, political journals, etc. made Gandhi a popular ﬁ gure. This was the ﬁ rst all India level Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi.

On April 13, 1919 the infamous Jallianwalla Bagh incident took place. On that day a large crowd gathered in the enclosed ground of Jallianwalla Bagh to protest against the Government’s new repressive measures and to protest against the arrest of two famous leaders of Punjab Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlu and Dr. Satyapal. Others had come to attend the annual Baisakhi fair. Being outside from the city, many villagers were unaware of the martial law that had been imposed. Dyer entered the area, blocked the exit points, and opened ﬁ re on the crowd, killing thousands of people.

The Committee had 7 members 4 British and 3 Indians. It was set up to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh Tragedy. Before the Committee could publish its report, Congress put forward its view. This view criticized Dyer’s act as inhuman and also said that there was no justiﬁ cation in the introduction of the martial law in Punjab. But the Hunter Report, as expected, saw the things differently. Although it condemned most of the decisions taken by Brigadier General Dyer, it agreed with the imposition of the martial law in Punjab. It also criticized the method of Satyagraha adopted by Gandhi and held Gandhi partially responsible for “deteriorated” law and order situation. On the recommendation of the commission, Rowlatt Act was passed in March, 1919. The Act empowered the Government to arrest any person without assigning any reason or ground for the arrest; search any place without a warrant and imprison any person without a trial. The Rowlatt Act raised a storm of protests and a wave of popular indignation throughout the country. The Press and the Congress called it the ‘Black Act.’ There were strikes and public meetings at various places throughout the country. At Amritsar, the arrest of Gandhiji and two prominent local leaders Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlu and Dr. Satyapal aroused a wave of protests. On April 13, 1919 a peaceful and unarmed protest rally was held in the open, but enclosed ground called Jallianwala Bagh. While the meeting was in progress, a British ofﬁ cer Brigadier General Dwyer along with his troops entered the park. Without any warning or asking the people to disperse, Brigadier General Dwyer and his troops started ﬁ ring at them. The park had a small exit gate; it too, was closed. In just ten minutes, about a thousand persons were killed, and many thousand wounded. The ﬁ ring stopped only after ammunition had been exhausted. It was led by Mahatma Gandhi after the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre and lasted from 1920 to February 1922. The non-cooperation movement was launched on 1 August 1920 and withdrawn in February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident. It was attended by most of the national leaders of the freedom struggle at the time and almost 300 other delegates from Bihar. The resolution was passed with a great majority. Under the resolution, people were advised to resign from administrative bodies and give up honorary title, withdraw children from Government Schools and College, refuse to attend ofﬁ cial event by the Government; boycott British courts and foreign goods and adopts Swadeshi goods and garments. Gandhi predicted that Swaraj would be attained in a year if the Non-cooperation movement was successful. The movement created ripples within the nation and provided the impetus to the nationalist movement.

अपने नमक सत्याग्रह के तहत, महात्मा गांधी: Under his Salt Satyagraha, Mahatma Gandhi reached Dandi village on April 5, 1930. While addressing the domestic and foreign journalists, he said: “I want world sympathy in this battle of Right against Might.”
दांडी के समुद्री तट पर नमक कानून का उल्ल: After violating the salt law at sea coast of Dandi, Gandhi decided to start the Civil Disobedience Movement. Salt was a major point of the Movement because the English Government had banned the selling of the salt and also imposed a tax on it, which highly affected the poor. Mahatma Gandhi started Dandi March accompanied by 80 of his trusted volunteers from Sabarmati Ashram on March 12, 1930. The march was 241 miles, from Gandhi’s ashram in Sabarmati to Gujarat's coastal town of Dandi. The volunteers walked for 24 days. On April 5, 1930 he reached Dandi, and ceremonially violated the salt law on 6th April, 1930. Thus, statement (c) is incorrect.

वेदारण्यम मार्च या वेदारण्यम सत्याग्रह क: The Vedaranyam March or Vedaranyam Satyagraha was organized to protest the Salt Tax imposed by the British Empire in India. The march took place in April, 1930 and was the second of its kind followed by Dandi March organized by Mahatma Gandhi, both in the framework of the Civil Disobedience Movement. The Vedaranyam March was a group of volunteers from under the leadership of C. Rajagopalachari. It began at Trichinopoly (now Tiruchirappalli) and ended in Vedaranyam, a small coastal town in Tanjore (in present day Vedaranyam beach of Nagapatinam district). By collecting salt directly from the sea, the marchers broke the Salt Law.

Gandhi-Irwin Pact *Viceroy Irwin released Gandhiji from Jail on 26th January 1931 considering the increasing inﬂ uence of the Civil Disobedience Movement. Talks between Gandhiji and Irwin started in February 1931 with the efforts of Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jaykar. Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5th March, 1931. Sarojani Naidu termed Irwin and Gandhiji as ‘Two Mahatmas’. According to this pact - (1) Under the leadership of Gandhiji congress decided to withdrew the civil disobedience movement, (2) All Prisoners of war who had no cases of the voilence to be released, (3) Right to peaceful protest at shops of foreign clothes and liquor shops, (4) Permission to make salt in the Coastal States without Salt Tax, (5) Congress agreed to participate in the Second Round Table Conference. People were disappointed by this Pact because this did not include the cancellation of the hanging of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. Biographer of Irwin, Alan Campbell Johnson termed the beneﬁ ts to Gandhi in Gandhi Irwin Pact as consolation prizes and said this Pact was the only surrender of Irwin agreeing for the conversation. 1. Quit India Movement *During 6-14 July, 1942, a meeting of Congress Committee was held at Wardha. It was attended by prominent leaders of Congress like Jawahar Lal Nehru, Abul Kalam Azad, Vallabh Bhai Patel, Mahatma Gandhi, Aruna Asaf Ali, Achyut Patwardhan, Dr. Anugrah Narayan Sinha, Pattabhi Sitaramaiyya etc. *‘Quit India’ resolution was passed in this meeting. It was chaired by then Congress President Abul Kalam Azad. *On 7th -8th August, 1942, annual meeting of All India Congress Committee was held at Gwaliya Tank of Bombay. Wardha Resolution was conﬁ rmed in this meeting. *After few modiﬁ cations, the resolution for Quit India movement was passed on 8th August, 1942. Quit India Movement for India’s Independence was launched on 9th August 1942. Gandhiji gave a statement before the ofﬁ cial launch of Quit India Movement. The statement had the following important points. 1) Government ofﬁ cials should announce their support and devotion to Congress. 2) Soldier should refuse to ﬁ re on their countrymen. 3) Students should quit studies only if they stood ﬁ rmly on this decision until independence. 4) Kings should accept the sovereignty of their people and declare their province as a part of the Indian Union. Masses should accept the leadership of the king only if he sees his future in the future of Masses. *In his speech Gandhiji said :- "I will not be satisﬁ ed with anything less than complete Independence". It may be possible that Salt Tax and Alcoholism, etc may be abolished or stopped by the English Government but my words will demand nothing less than complete independence. Today I give you a mantra “Do or Die”. This mantra means that either we will free our country or will die ﬁ ghting for Independence. *On 8th August, 1942, Jawahar Lal Nehru presented the ‘Quit India resolution’ to All India Congress Committee. This proposal was supported by Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel. The draft of this porposal was prepared by Mahatma Gandhi himself with the help of Jawahar lal and Abul Kalam Azad. *Hindu Mahasabha, Communist Party of India, Unionist Party (Punjab) and Muslim League were not in favour of this movement. On 9th August, 1942, Quit India Movement was launched. In the early hours of the Movement, Gandhiji and other important leaders of Congress were arrested under operation zero hour. *Gandhiji and Sarojini Naidu were arrested and taken to Aga Khan Palace. *Members of Congress Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Abul Kalam Azad, Govind Ballabh Pant, Dr. Prafful Chandra Ghosh, Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramaiyya, Dr. Sayyed Mehmood, Acharya Kriplani) were arrested and taken to Ahmednagar Fort. *Dr. Rajendra Prasad, member of Congress working Committee couldn't come to Bombay, he was arrested and kept at Patna (Bankipur) Jail. Shivkumar and Ramanand were arrested in Hazaribagh. *Movement of 1942 showed maximum impact in Bombay, Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, United Province and Madras but the participation of the whole country was necessary for this movement to succeed. *Lord Wavell was the commander in chief of India during Quit India Movement (1942). He was elected President in Ramgarh Session of Congress in 1940 and after that for ﬁ ve years (1941- 45) no session of Congress was held and Abul Kalam Azad continued to be the President of Congress for these years. He was the President of Congress for the maximum years before independence, also the political scenario of India was very fragile during his tenure. *During Quit India Movement, a secret radio station of Congress was broadcasted from different parts of Bombay which can be heard upto Madras. Ram Manohar Lohia broadcasted from that radio frequently. *Usha Mehta was an important member of the group of Congress that broadcasted radio being underground. *Louis Fischer, an American journalist, was with Gandhiji during Quit India Movement. (He was Biographer of Gandhiji). *Louis Fischer with American intellectuals Pearl Buck, Adgersnow, M.L. Surmen and Norman Thomas demanded India’s Independence. *Riots emerging out of Quit India Movement were widespread in Bihar and United Province It emerged as a revolt. Eastern United Province including Azamgarh, Ballia, Gorakhpur, and Gaya, Champaran, Saran, Purnia, Shahabad, Muzaffarpur, and Bhagalpur areas of Bihar were self instilled centres of mass revolt. *August Movement of 1942 became widespread amongst the farmers. ब्रिटिश ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के भारतीय क्षे: Regulating Act, 1773, was passed by the British Parliament for the regulation of the British East India Company’s Indian Territories, mainly in Bengal. The main provisions of the Act were the appointment of a Governor-General of Fort William in Bengal with supervisory powers over the Presidencies of Madras (now Chennai) and Bombay (now Mumbai). The Governor-General had a Council of four who were given the power to cast a vote but no veto. Warren Hastings was appointed the ﬁ rst Governor General of Bengal.
रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट, (1773) ने फोर्ट विलियम,: The Regulating Act, (1773), established India’s ﬁ rst Supreme Court, at Fort William, Calcutta. This Supreme Court consisted of a Chief Justice and three other regular Judges or Puisne Judges. Sir Elijah Impey was the ﬁ rst Chief Justice. The Supreme Court was the supreme judiciary over all British subjects including the provinces of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. The Supreme Court came into force in 1774.
1786 में, कॉर्नवालिस को बंगाल का गवर्नर-: In 1786, another bill was brought in the Parliament relating to India in a bid to prevail upon Cornwallis to accept the Governor-General of Bengal. Cornwallis wanted to have the power of both the Governor-General and the Commander- in-Chief. The provisions of the Act were that the Governor- General in special cases relating to peace, defence or well- being of Indian empire, had the power to override the majority of the Council and enforce their rule.
कॉर्नवालिस के न्यायिक सुधारों ने 1793 मे: Cornwallis judicial reforms took the ﬁ nal shape in 1793 and were embodied in the famous Cornwallis Code. The new reforms were based on the principle of Separation of Powers. Under the inﬂ uence of the eighteenth-century French philosophers, Cornwallis sought to separate the revenue administration from the administration of justice. The Collector was the head of the revenue department in a district and also enjoyed extensive judicial and magisterial powers. Cornwallis believed that concentration of all powers in the hands of the Collector in the District retards the improvement as a judge of the Diwani Adalat redress the wrongs done by him as collector or assessor of revenue? Thus, neither the landlords nor the cultivators could regard the Collector as an impartial Judge in revenue cases. The Cornwallis Code divested the Collector of all judicial and magisterial powers and left him with the duty of administration of revenue. A new class of ofﬁ cer called the District Judge was created to preside over the District Civil Court. The District Judge was empowered with magisterial and police functions.
1813 के चार्टर अधिनियम द्वारा भारत के व्: The monopoly of East India Company in India’s trade was abolished by the Charter Act of 1813. But they held the monopoly on the trade of Tea and trade with China.
काहर्टर एक्ट, 1813 ने ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी: The cahrter act, 1813 compelled the East India company to assert the responsibility for the education of the Indian. It made a provision for an annual grant of a sum of 1 lakh rupees for the promotion of education in India.
चार्टर अधिनियम, 1833 को इस शर्त पर नवीनी: The Charter Act, 1833, was renewed on the condition that Company should abandon its trade entirely, alike with India and China and permit Europeans to settle freely in India. The Company lost its monopoly in China and also the trade of tea which it enjoyed with the Charter Act of 1813. Governor- General of Bengal was made the Governor-General of British India with this Act, and all ﬁ nancial and administrative powers were centralized in the hands of Governor-General- in-Council. The 4th member was not entitled to act as a member of the Council except for legislative purposes. A British member was appointed as a Law Member in the Governor-General’s Council. A ﬁ rst fourth person appointed as the Member of the Council was Lord Macaulay. Thus option (d) is the correct answer.
मोंटागु-चेम्सफोर्ड रिपोर्ट ने प्रशासन मे: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report recommended to increase the number of Indians in administration and also recommended that the examination shall be jointly held in Britain and India for Civil Services. On their recommendation, the Civil Services was held together in England and India from 1922. The Aitchison Commission submitted its report in 1887. The Commission opposed to the demand of the simultaneous holding, in England as well as in India.
चार्टर अधिनियम, 1853 में प्रावधान था कि: The Charter Act, 1853 provided that the salary of the members of Board of Control, its Secretary and other Ofﬁ cers would be ﬁ xed by the Bri tish Government but the payments would be made out of the Com pany’s funds. The number of the Directors of the Court of Directors was re duced from 24 to 18 of whom 6 were to be nominated by the Crown. The Court of Directors was divested of its right to patronage and Company’s services were thrown open to competition and no dis crimination of any kind was to be made. A Committee with Macau lay was formed in the following year (1854) to give effect to the scheme of appointment in Civil Services through competition.
1853 के चार्टर अधिनियम द्वारा कार्यपालिक: A decisive step had been initiated in the separation of powers between the Executive and the Legislature by the Charter Act of 1853. It was the ﬁ rst time in India when the Legislative Council was established. The total number of the members in the Legislative Council was 12.
1922 से भारत में ICS परीक्षा आयोजित की ज: 1922 onwards, ICS exam began to be held in India. In 1924, Lee Commission had recommended in its report for the establishment of an independent and impartial Public Service Commission for India and on the basis of such recommendation, the Public Service Commission was established in 1926. Subsequently by the Government of India Act, 1935, Public Service Commission were established separately for both the Central and the State Government Services. Under this act, Federal Public Service Commission was formed in Place of Public Service Commission.

1919 का मोंटागु-चेम्सफोर्ड सुधार भारत मे: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reform of 1919 was introduced by the British Government in India to introduce self-governing institutions gradually to India. In this ‘Dyarchy in the Provinces’ was introduced. Reserved subjects like Finance, Law and order, Army, Police, etc. Transferred subjects like Public health, educations, agriculture, Local Self-Government, etc. The reserved subjects were kept with the Governor and his executive council. While the administration of the transferred subjects was handed over to the ministers responsible to the Provincial legislative.

History) 2014 49 Explanation- The ruins of Mohenjodaro, the ancient site of Indus Valley Civilization, are located on the right bank of the Indus River in Larkana district of Sindh province of Pakistan. The mounds of Mohenjodaro are spread over an area of ​​about five kilometers. The credit for the exploration of the mounds of Mohenjodaro in 1922 goes to Rakhaldas Banja. The residential houses of Mohenjodaro were built with baked bricks. There is no information yet about the mausoleum area (if there was any) from Mohenjodaro. Two types of evidence of dead bodies have been found inside the city of Mohenjodaro - (a) partial burial, (c) complete cremation (dpanana). Bones of birds, fish etc., coal and ash, dead bodies, jewelery etc. were found inside. Some scholars have considered these to be examples of partial burial. Under the second category, forty-two skeletons recovered from the last phase of Mohenjodaro can be placed, which were found lying in a disorganized condition inside houses and on public roads in the city area.

On the basis of human skeletons found in disorganized condition from the upper surface of Mohenjodaro, it was concluded that there was an invasion from the west during the last period of the Indus Valley civilization. Scholars have linked the evidence of female figures depicted on statues and seals found in archaeological sites associated with the Harappan civilization to the worship of matriarchal power. According to Marshall and Martha Miller, the mother goddess had the highest position in the family of gods of the Indus Valley civilization. On the basis of evidence obtained from the ancient sites of Indus Valley civilization, it is proved that the residents here used to worship Shiva, Peepal, Naga etc.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2003 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2003 Explanation- Burjheim is an important site of the Neolithic period. It is located in Kashmir province. An ancient site named Burzheim was discovered in 1935 AD. It was done by De Terra and Peterson. 1960-64 AD This place was excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India between. Excavations at Burzheim have revealed remains of pit houses and the site is famous for its pit dwellings. The shape of the troughs is narrower towards the top and wider towards the bottom. The Neolithic culture was more developed than its predecessor cultures. The man of this period was not only a consumer of food systems but also became their producer. He was completely familiar with agricultural work. Along with agriculture, humans also started rearing animals. His acquaintance with animals like cow, buffalo, bull, horse, sheep, goat etc. increased.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2008 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2008 Explanation─ Seals have an important place in the field of established art of Harappan civilization. Developed sculpture can be seen on the seals. The shape of seals is mainly square or rectangular. Square seals were the most popular. Statues of Taurus, elephant, gad, tiger, leaves, twigs etc. have been carved in great detail on the seals using very sharp and precise tools. The seals are mostly made of alabaster. Copper seals have been found from Lothal and Deshalpur.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 Explanation – Chanhudaro is the only ancient site from where curved bricks have been found and no fort has been found from Chanhudaro. Only a small part of this settlement has been excavated. Among the important construction works found here was a bead making factory. The western mound enclosed by the fort in Kalibanga has two separate but interconnected sections. One was probably for the residence of a special section of the population and the other for several raised platforms on whose tops there is evidence of the existence of fire pits. The entire settlement in Lothal was surrounded by a wall. This was a well-planned settlement, a pond-like enclosure made of baked bricks is found in the eastern section of Lothal. Surkotad shows a repetition of the plan of the western mound of Kalibanga. There is no eastern mound at this site. There is a cemetery to the west of the western mound of Kalibanga and in the east there is evidence of a structure where perhaps rituals were performed. The plan of the eastern mound of Kalibanga is similar to the plan of Mohenjodaro but the difference between the two is that the houses of Kalibanga were made of mud bricks.

During the excavations conducted under the direction of Brajwasi Lal and Balkrishna Thapar, antiquities of Proto-Harappan and Harappan civilization were discovered.

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2001 Explanation- Sutkagender, an ancient site associated with the Harappan culture, is located in the Balochistan province of Pakistan. The sites of Balochistan are generally found along trade routes. For example, it seems that there are many such sites on the Makran Coast region. Here the geographical elements are important. First, many rivers meet the sea in this area. The mouth of these rivers can be considered a convenient place. The settlements which are found today a few miles away from the sea were on the sea shore, hence these settlements had the advantage of Dehra, because they were situated at the mouth of the river and also on the shore of the sea. Of these, three sites are important from archaeological point of view - Sutkagender (at the mouth of Dashk River), Sotkakoh (at the mouth of Shadi Kor) and Balakot (at the mouth of Vidar River, east of Son Miyani Gulf). The fort of this city was surrounded by a stone wall and it is known as a port of the Indus period.

There is relatively more evidence available regarding trade after the Indus Valley Civilization. The cities of the Indus Valley Civilization had close trade relations with the countries of Central and Western Asia. Evidence of trade contacts of Indus cities with Afghanistan, Soviet Russia, South Turkmenistan, Persian Gulf countries, Iran and Iraq has been found. Lajwad and silver were imported from Afghanistan. Badakhsha region of Afghanistan is very famous for Lajwad. Antiquities of the Indus Valley Civilization have been found during the excavation of an ancient site called Shotugai in Afghanistan. Indus Valley Civilization is not otherwise spread in this region of Afghanistan. Therefore Shotugui can be considered an intermediate trading settlement.

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 UPPC: UPPCS (झृ) घृघः History, 2002 UPPCS (ःृ) ःृष्ठ History, 2008 Explanation- Lagadh Muni is famous as the author of 'Vedang-Jyotish'. He had composed Arya Astrology related to Tri + Gveda and Yajush-Jyotish related to Yajuvxad. 'Yajush' means 'yajna'. Therefore, in the Yajuvad Samhita, useful mantras have been collected for performing the yagyas, which were chanted by the Adhvayu priest on the occasion of the yagya. Yajuvad is ritualistic. It gives details of the methods of performing Yagya. Yajuvad has two parts – Krishna Yajuvad and Shukyal Yajuvad. Krishna Yajuvad contains rhymed mantras and lyrical sentences, whereas Shukyal Yajuvad contains only mantras. Both of them have many branches. The main branches of Krishna Yajuvad are Taittiriya, Kathak, Maitrayani and Kapisthala. The main branches of Shukyal Yajuvad are Madhyanindna and Kanva. The Samhitas of Shukyal Yajuvad are also called 'Vajasaneya' because Vajasaneyi's son Yajnavalkya was the seer of them. It has a total of forty chapters.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2007 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2007 Explanation - In 'Vedtrayee' mainly three Vedas, Tri-Gveda, Yajuvad and Samaveda are counted. Of these, Tra+gveda is a collection of mantras which were sung on the occasion of yagyas. 'Yajuvad' contains a collection of mantras useful for performing Yagyas, which were chanted by the 'Adhvayu' priest on the occasion of Yagya. Yajuvad is ritualistic in which details of the methods of performing Yagya are given. Samveda contains a collection of mantras sung on the occasion of Yagya. The person who sang these mantras was called 'Udgata'. These three Vedas together are called 'Vedtrayee'.

It was the responsibility of the Brahmin priests to perform this Yagya. These Brahmin priests were of four types - (1) Heta or Hetri – He was the knower of Tri + Gveda. He used to worship the deities through mantras by pouring fire in the Yagya Kund. (2) Udgata – He was a knowledgeable Heta of Samveda. He used to sing Soma in the Yagya. (3) Adhvayu or Yagnik – He was an expert in Yajuvad who used to perform the methods of Yagnik rituals. (4) Bramya – Its role was that of an inspector at the time of Yagya.

After this, five rivers of Punjab – Indus, Vitast (Jhelum), Askini (Chenab), Parushni (Ravi), Vipasa (Beas) have been mentioned. Along with this, names of Shatudri (Sutlej), Saraswati, Yamuna and Ganga are also found.

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2007 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2007 Explanation – In the Vedas, there is mention of these three officers – Purohit, Senani and Gramani. Out of this, the priest used to accompany the king to the battlefield and pray for the king's victory in the war. In a way, he was the king's teacher, guide and friend. The commander was the most important officer of the army and on the occasion of war, he worked as per the orders of the king. During winter, the soldier probably had to perform civilian duties as well. 'Gramani' was the head of the village and the village leader for administrative and military functions. He represented the interests of the rural people.

Polygamy and widow remarriage were prevalent. There is mention of 10 wives of Manu in Maitrayani Samhita. Women were given adequate education. PGT History्, 2004 व्याख्या – त्र+ग्वेद: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – In Tra + Gveda the word Dharma is used in the meaning of method (थाय). This has nothing to do with morality. UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- Most of the Yagyas of the Vedic period were performed on special occasions and festivals. Drsha Yagya was performed on Amavasya day, while Pournmas Yagya was performed on Poonima day. We get definite knowledge about the religion of ancient Indians first of all from Vedic literature. In which Vedas, Brahmanas, Natha, Aranyakas and Upanishads are counted. The oldest of this literature is 'Tra+gveda'. In which we first see polytheism. The Aryans believed in the existence of various deities. Most of their deities are symbols of various forces of nature which have been personified and it is believed that the activities of the world are governed by the mercy of the gods. Each deity is depicted as the creator and controller of the world. There is mention of mantras chanted towards various deities in the Vedas. In the yagyas, offerings of fire, water, food, meat etc. were made and the gods themselves were present and offered the offerings. The main deities of Drsha Yagya were 'Agni and Indra' and the main deities of the full month were 'Agni and Som'.
(Uउण Nू.-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह, 2015) व्याख्: (Uun Nu.-घुघ्घ झाजी वल्ह, 2015) Explanation – The Yajnavalkya-Gagaa dialogue mentioned in the Vridharanyaka Upanishad, on the one hand, shows that some women in the society could attain higher education, but it also indicates that perhaps there were limits to that too. PGT History्, 2009 UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह: PGT History, 2009 UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2005 Explanation – Mainly three cities are mentioned in the Vedic period literature in which Ayodhya has been described in the Atharva Veda. Both Yadu and Turvasu were the chieftains of the Tri-Gveda period. Bharat Jana was older than them. For example, the Yadu and Turvas castes were undoubtedly counted among the Aryan Panchmanushas. But these have also been called ten at one place. The sounds of the names of two important heroes of the Vedas, Divodas and Sudas, are no less important. From the point of view of philology, names of ten like Shambar, Shushna, Tugu, Vetsu, Chumari, Abud do not appear to be non-Aryan. It has been said about ten people that they neither offered sacrifices in the fire nor were they partial to Indra-Varun. Dasyus have been described as Adevayu (those who do not have faith in deities), Abrahan (those who do not believe in the Vedas) and Ayjvan (those who do not perform Yagya). Overall, in the Tri + Gveda, Dsyuas and AyaX have been described as bigger enemies than the Dasas.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2001 Explanation- Oriental is in the east. According to Aitareya Brahman, the kings of the eastern direction (Magadha, Kalinga and Banga etc.) are anointed for the empire and are called 'Emperor'. UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 Explanation- In the Vedas, the names of women like Ghosha, Lopamudra, Vishvavara, etc. are mentioned, who were well educated and who had also composed some mantras. Women had the same social and religious rights as men, but the Vedic society considered them ineligible due to two disadvantages: (a) They did not have the right to participate in politics. (अ) They did not have property related rights. In other respects they were equal to men. In the Vedic society, marriage was considered a sacred bond. In Shatpath Brahman, the wife has been called the husband's concubine. She could participate in the yagya along with her husband, a person without a wife was not entitled to perform the yagya. In the Vedas, its importance has been clearly accepted by saying 'Jayedstam' i.e. the wife is the home. The practice of monogamous marriage was generally prevalent in the family, although some people of the elite class had multiple wives. Child marriage and widow remarriage were not allowed. The main purpose of marriage was to have a son. There were constant prayers for the abundance of sons.

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- Kumaril, a follower of Mimamsa philosophy, supported Vedic Yagya. In Mimamsa philosophy (followed by Prabhakar and Kumarila), Vedic rituals have been given utmost importance and have been described as mandatory for every person. Mimamsaka advises to properly perform the Yagyas prescribed in the Vedas and their rituals. Religion has great importance in Mimamsa philosophy. According to Jaimini (the pioneer of Mimamsa philosophy), religion is the command which inspires man to work. Knowledge of religion comes only from Apaurusheya Vedas. What the Vedas prescribe is Dharma, what it prohibits is Adharma. We can attain Dharma only by behaving according to the rules of Vedas. Mimamsa philosophy gives importance only to action which is capable of providing moments with its power (Apoorva). For this they do not consider the power of God necessary. The views of Mimamsakas regarding God are not clear. The main goal of this philosophy is to propound the importance of karma.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2007 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2007 Explanation - In the Vedic period, the condition of women was better as compared to the later Vedic period. They had the right to participate in religious activities. There was no practice of child marriage and women were married only after attaining adulthood. Its impact was positive for women and they got the opportunity to get adequate education. Literary evidence indicates that there were some learned women of this period who composed Vedic hymns. These tri+chayas are stored in Tri+gveda. Lopa, Ghosha, Apala, Vishwavara etc. were prominent among these women.

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2006 87 व: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2006 87 Explanation: Yajuvad is a compilation of Yajus. The literal meaning of 'Yajush' is Yagya, Puja, Shraddha, Adra etc. The mantras of this Veda are recited in the yagya by a priestly class called Adhvayu. Its Vajasaneyi Samhita has 40 chapters. The first 25 chapters are very important from the point of view of the subject matter. In the first and second chapters, the mantras of 'Drsha' and 'Purnmas' yagyas are compiled. The third chapter contains a collection of mantras for the daily 'Agnihetra' and 'Chaturmasya' yagya. From the fourth to the eighth chapter, we get mantras related to 'Agnishtomadi' Somayajnas and animal sacrifice. Several yagyas that end in one day are also found in the tradition of Somayyagyas. Among these, Vajpayee Yagya is most prominent. In the same tradition as Somayyagyas, there is Rajasuya Yagya performed by the kings. The prayers for Vajpayee and Rajasuya Yagyas have been given in the ninth and tenth chapters of Vajasaneyi Samhita. It is noteworthy that in Tri+Gvaidic religion, the deities were worshiped by performing yagya to get their blessings or blessings. The sacrifices given in the yagyas were milk, sugar, ghee, meat and soma. There is detailed mention of only Som Yagya in Tri + Veda.

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 Explanation- As simple as the social and economic life of the Gvaidic period was, the religious life was equally complex. Here we initially find visions of 'polytheism'. The principal deities of Ayax are representatives of natural forces personified. Tri+Gvaidic deities have been classified into three parts - (a) Gods of the earth - Gods of earth, fire, Soma, Jupiter and rivers etc. (अ) Gods of space- Indra, Rudra, Vayu, Vaat, Parjanya, Aapah, Maat, Rishwan Aditi etc. (M) Gods of the sky – Ghaus (Aaus), Varun, Mitra Surya, Savitri Pushan, Vishnu, Aditya, Usha, Ashwin etc. Tri+Gvaidic deities are mainly male deities. Sometimes deities are also imagined in animal form. For example, Indra or Ghaus (Aaus) has been depicted as a Taurus and Surya as a horse, but it would not be appropriate to understand from this that the Tri+Gvaidic Aryans worshiped animals also. The belief of considering any animal as an ancestor, sacred and a deity is not found in the Tri + Gveda, but in the Tri + Gveda, a deity named Pushand has been praised. Pushan was the god of roads, shepherds and animals and his chariot was drawn by goats.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2010 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2010 Explanation – In Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, Ajatashatru has been called the king of Kashi. Aेप्araस झ्addप्aूग थम्ू. Exaस. 2012 व्य: अप्रास झड़पुग थम्ू. Exas. 2012 Explanation – There are two parts of Yajuvda. Shukyal Yajuvad and Krishna Yajuvad. Shukyal Yajuvxad is known as Vajasaneyi Samhita and the word 'Hiranyakar' is found in it.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2009 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2009 Explanation─The main basis of Indian philosophy and the last section of Vedic literature are Upanishads, they are also called Vedanta. The total number of Upanishads is 108. Which is mentioned in 'Muktikopanishad'. Out of which there are 13 important Upanishads. Of these, De─Etreya and Kaushitaki are related to Tri + Gveda, De─Chhandegya and Ken are related to Samaveda, four─Taittiriya, Kath, Shwetashvatara and Maitrayani are related to Krishna Yajuvad, De─Bridharanyaka and Ish are related to Shukyal Yajuvad, and three─Mundak, Prashna and Mandukya are related to Atharvaveda. Is. Kath, Shwetashvatara, Ish and Mundak Upanishads are in rhyme, while some parts of Ken and Prashna Upanishad are in rhyme and some are in Ga. The remaining seven Upanishads are in Ga. Hence Brihadaranyaka Upanishad is in Ga.

It is said in Shatapatha Brahmana that 'Videha Madhav had held Vaishvantar fire in his mouth. As soon as Dhritra's name was taken, the fire came out of Madhav's mouth and reached the earth. At that time Videh Madhav lived on the banks of Saraswati. Burning everything with fire, he moved towards the east and behind him came Vidhemadhav and his priest Gautam Rahugaan. UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2005 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2005 Explanation – During the Upanishad period, there were many kings who were keen on Brahma knowledge and spiritual consciousness. Janaka of Videha, Ashwapati of Kaikeya, Ajatashatru of Kashi and Pravana Javali of Panchal country etc. are famous, whereas according to Janmejaya Shatapath Brahman, there was a king of Kuru dynasty whose capital was Asandivat. Aेप्araस झ्addप्aूग थम्ू. Exaस. 2012 व्य: अप्रास झड़पुग थम्ू. Exas. 2012 Explanation – Meṇḍadiki is related to the Mahayana branch of Buddhism. In this, an attempt has been made to bind the entire world in one thread by considering the principles of Buddha and Bodhisattva as the central point. Traditionally, someone who is motivated by great compassion, born with bodhicitta, and attains enlightenment through spontaneous desire for the benefit of all sentient beings is considered a bodhisattva.

In Tra+Gvaidic the terms Go and Vrishabha have been used 176 and 170 times respectively. The horse was the second important animal domesticated by the early settlers. Horses have been praised in detailed hymns of the Vedas. It seems that in the Tri+Gvaidic cattle rearing society, the chiefs of the clan had dominance over horse riding. UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History Edt., 2004 Explanation- In the pre-Vedic period, people lived in groups, that is, the group took the form of a clan and the land on which they lived was the land of the entire clan. The king was not the master of the land but the master of war.

Later, there was a war with King Sudas and 10 other kings, which included 5 Aryas and 5 chieftains of Ayattar tribes. King Sudas was victorious in this war. UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – There was a provision for the use of 25 Yupas in Purushamedha, while there were 21 Yupas in Vajpayee Yagya and 16 Yupas in Ashwamedha Yagya. A detailed study of important yagyas of this era like Ashwamedha, Vajpayee, Rajasuya etc. shows that basically its purpose was to increase agricultural production. Vajpayee was not only related to food and drinks but also Ashvamedha and Rajsuya which are considered to be the sources of so-called political power. There were many such customs and symbols. There is important mention in Vridharanyaka Upanishad and Vajasaneyi Samhita regarding such activities in Vajpayee Yagya.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2010 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2010 Explanation – Animal husbandry was the main industry of Ayahuasca during the Vedic period. Prayers were offered to the gods for the growth of livestock. Cow had the utmost importance. It was calculated in economic terms. Goods were purchased through the exchange of cows. Buffalo was also a domesticated animal for milk, meat and skin. In the Vedas, buffalo has been called Gowal. Aryan people were also familiar with sheep and goat. Horse was the most useful animal of AyaX which was used in his war. Horse meat was also given in the south and sometimes its meat was also eaten. Aryans also used elephants in battle. Along with horses and carts, oxen were also used to pull carts and chariots. Dog, pig, donkey and deer were also prominent among the domesticated animals.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह, 2011) व्याख्य: (Uun Nu.- घुघ झजाजी वल्ह, 2011) Explanation – In the Vedas, Panchjana refers to the five tribes of AayaX. According to Vedic mythology, there were five tribes i.e. Jana. These five tribes were Anu, Druh, Puru, Turvasu and Yadu. The ruler of these tribes was called Janapati or Raja.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह, 2015) व्याख्य: (Uun Nu.- घघ झजाजी वल्ह, 2015) Explanation – Gayatri Mantra is mentioned in the third chapter of Tri+Gveda. Gayatri Mantra was compiled by priest Vishwamitra. When the sun starts shining then it is called Savita. The famous Gayatri Mantra of Tri-Gveda is dedicated to Savita only.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 86 व: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 86 Explanation- The first agronomist mentioned in Atharvaveda was Prithuvainya (god of agriculture) who first gave birth to plow and agriculture. Atharvaveda Samhita is about giving cosmic moments, it mentions the rituals performed to make human life happy and free from sorrow. A sage named Atharva is its first seer. Hence, it has been named Atharvaveda in his name. Its second vision is Angiras Tri+Rishi. For this reason this Veda is also called Athangiras Veda. Mantras related to various subjects like disease prevention, tantramantra, magic, curse, vashikaran, blessings, praise for long life, beauty, rain, atonement, marriage, love, royal deeds, importance of motherland etc. are also found in Atharvaveda. It is also full of many things about the principles and practice of Ayurveda. In this way, this book is an encyclopedia of worldly conduct and conduct. Even from the beginning of Kalpa, this is a high quality collection in which very beautiful and highly touching songs and poems have been included.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी अम. 2015) व्याख्या: (Uun No.- घुघ झाजी Am. 2015) Explanation- Bhikshuni Sangha was established by Mahavir Swami on the request of public opinion. At the time of the primary Sangha, Mahavira had one lakh sixty nine thousand Shravakas (monks) and three lakh eighteen thousand Shravikas (bhikshunis). It was the largest religious association in the world at that time. The monks' union was led by Indrabhuti and the head of the nuns' union was princess Chandnabala (Chandna).
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2010 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2010 Explanation – Regarding the Angic Path, Mahatma Buddha says to Anand that O Anand, at this time I have also established this Kalyanvartya i.e. Kalyanmitra, which is for solitude, for detachment, for cessation, for alleviation, for abhijna, for enlightenment and for Nirvana, this is the Arya Angic Path. In fact, it is considered necessary to follow the Angic path for every means because attaining Nirvana was possible only through this.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2003 UPPC: UPPCS (झृ) घुह्गाह History, 2003 UPPCS (झृ) घुह्गाह History, (Edt.) 2004 Explanation- Vaishnav religion developed from Bhagwat religion. According to tradition, its originator was Krishna of Vrishna (Satvat) lineage, who is called Vasudev Krishna because he was the son of Vasudev. He was originally a resident of Mathura. In Chhandegya Upanishad, he has been described as the son of Devki and the disciple of Ghor Angiras. Krishna's followers call him 'Bhagwat'. For this reason the religion promoted by him came to be known as Bhagwat. During the Mahabharata period, 'Vasudev Krishna' was equated with Vishnu. Vishnu of Bhagwat religion is a Tri + Vedic deity and is a god of nature like other deities. They represent the active form of the Sun. Vishnu is most important because he measured the entire earth with three steps. He has been described as Urugaya (one with great speed) and 'Urukam' (one with wide foot projections). 124

In which the first was Tri+Shabhadev or Adinath and the 23rd was Parshvanath.
: बुद्ध शब्द का शीबि्द्क अर्थ है 'प्रबुद: : The literal meaning of the word Buddha is 'enlightened'. Buddha is one who has attained Bodhi and Bodhi means an ideal state of enlightenment, intellectual and moral perfection that can be achieved by man through purely human means. After six years of tireless hard work and severe penance, at the age of 35, Siddhartha attained enlightenment on the banks of the Niranjana (Punpun) river under a Peepal tree on one night of Vaishakh Purnima. From this day onwards he became a Tathagat. After attaining enlightenment, Gautam became famous by the name of 'Buddha'.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह, 2015) 131 व: (Uun No.- घुघ्घ झाजी वल्ह, 2015) 131 Explanation – During the war of Ajatashatru against Chetak, the ruler of Vaishali, Ajatashatru's minister Vatsakar met Buddha in Rajgriha. Its mention is found in the Buddhist text 'Mahaparinivvan Sutta'. From this connection it is known that Ajatashatru consulted Mahatma Buddha and it was he who told him that the destruction of Vajji Sangha is possible only through discrimination. Thereafter, he sent his minister Vatsakar and created a split in the Wajij Sangh.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History Edition, 2004 Explanation- Shankaracharya, the famous Hindu thinker of the 8th century, who vehemently opposed Buddhism and established Sanatan Dharma. : महवीर ने कड़ी तपस्या के पातd वैशाख शुक: : Mahavir, after rigorous penance, remained in meditation for twelve years, 5 months and 15 days in Gauduh Asana on the banks of river Tra+Jupalika in Jrimbhak village of Magadha in the fourth quarter of Vaishakh Shukyal Dashami, when he attained spiritual knowledge (Kaivalya).

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2006 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2006 Explanation: In Jainism, 'Sallekhana' means sacrifice through fasting. Maurya emperor Chandragupta Maurya converted to Jainism in the last days of his life. At the end of his reign there was a famine of 12 years in Magadha. Failing to deal with the famine situation, Chandragupta Maurya abdicated Esahasan in favor of his son and went to Shravanabelagola (Mysore) to do penance with Bhadrabahu. It was at this very place that he sacrificed his life in the Sallekhana ritual.
: बौद्ध महसभा का क्ुल 4 बार उल्लेख मिलता: : Buddhist Mahasabha is mentioned a total of 4 times, in which the first Buddhist council took place in Rajagriha during the reign of Ajatashatru, which was presided over by Mahakassapa. The second Buddhist council was held in Vaishali under the chairmanship of Sarbkami (Savakamir) during the reign of Kalashoka, the third Buddhist council was organized in Patliputra under the chairmanship of Mogaliputtatisya during the reign of Ashoka and the fourth Buddhist council was held in Kundalvan of Kashmir under the chairmanship of Vasumitra during the reign of Kanishka.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2011 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2011 Explanation – The principle of 'Pratityasamutpada' is related to Buddhism. Just as birth is the cause of the accumulation of sorrow, similarly the cause of birth is also the cycle of ignorance that gives rise to the results of karma, which in the terminology is called pratityasamutpad (or paticchasammupada in Pali language), i.e. 'pratatya' (from its existence) samutpad (it arises). There are 12 sequences of this cycle, which cause each other to arise, these are – (1) Aviya, (2) Sanskar, (3) Vijnana, (4) Nama-paripa, (5) Shadayatan, (6) Sparsha, (7) Vedna, (8) Trishna, (9) Upadana, (10) Bhava, (11) Jati (12) Jara-Maran. 129
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2010 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2010 Explanation – Udayin or Udyabhadra had founded a city named Patliputra. Udayin shifted his capital from Rajagriha by establishing the city of Patliputra at the exact confluence of Ganga and Son. Which was covered by a perimeter. Gates were made to enter it and soldiers with archers were deployed to protect the city.

PGT History्, 2004 व्याख्या – मह्षि वेद्: PGT History, 2004 Explanation – The epic Mahabharata written by Mahishi Vedvyas initially had only 8800 verses and its name was 'Jayasamhita' (the text related to victory). Later, when the number of verses increased to 24000, it became famous by the name 'Bharat'. Over time, it contained 100,000 verses and it came to be known as 'Shatasahstri Samhita' or 'Mahabharata'.
Uउण NET-घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–का: Uun NET-घुझ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – Kaalx is situated in Pune (Poona) district of Maharashtra. Here a chaitya has been built by cutting the mountain, which is the largest and most beautiful among all the excavated chaitya houses of India. It is 124 feet 3 inches long, 45 feet 5 inches wide and 46 feet high. There is a huge pillar at the entrance of the group on which four lions are sitting. There are three entrances to enter the pavilion. Kalax is the most elaborate and developed psychic house of Hinayana period. It was built in the Satavahana era (around the first century BC). There is an article about it here itself, according to which a businessman named Bhootpal of Vaijayanti had got it constructed.
: बौद्ध संघ में उपसंपद संघ में प्रविष्ट: : In the Buddhist Sangha, one was asked to enter the Upasampada Sangha. After giving his first sermon at Sarnath, Buddha founded the Sangha with 5 Brahmin disciples. The organization of the Buddhist Sangha was based on the Gantinitrak system. UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 Explanation- During his religious preaching journey, Gautam Buddha went to Sumasumaragiri, the capital of Bhaggo and spent the eighth year there. Here Bodhi Kumar became his disciple. From here he went to Kaushambi, the capital of Vatsaraja Udyan and took rest there. From here Buddha went to Berenza near Mathura where he stayed for the twelfth year. King Prasota of Avanti also invited him but he expressed his inability to go there due to his old age and asked his disciple Mahakachayana to preach to him. Even in Avanti, some followers of Buddha became there. Buddha also traveled to Champa and Kajangal and stayed in those places for some time and initiated many people into his faith. Buddhism was propagated most in Kosala state. Buddha lived here twenty-one. A very rich businessman named Anathapindak accepted his discipleship.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History एजट., 2004 Explanation- In the Buddhist Tripitaka, there is mention of sixteen Mahajanapadas in Anguttarnikaya, a part of Sutta Pitaka and in Jain «Nth Bhagwati Sutra. There is mention of Angulimala in Anguttarnikaya and about the lives of Jain Tirthankaras in Bhagwati Sutra.

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2006 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2006 Explanation: Buddhism entered Tibet in the fourth century. In the 8th century, the Tibetan king invited an Indian teacher named Shantarakshita to come to Tibet. With the help of Acharya Pa Sambhava, Shantarakshita propagated Buddhism in Tibet. Shantarakshita was a teacher of the Sarvistavadi sect. He called 12 other monks from India for his cooperation and due to their efforts Tibetan people started becoming Buddhist monks. Pasambhava believed in tantric teachings, due to his efforts Vrajyana entered Tibet.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2001 Explanation- In the beginning of 6th century BC, there was complete lack of sovereign power in North India. The entire region was divided into many independent states. No ruler of this period was capable of organizing political unity. The authentic description of the political situation of this period is not available from any literary evidence, however, it is known from the Buddhist 'Nth Anguttara Nikaya' that before the rise of Mahatma Gautam Buddha, the whole of Northern India was divided into 16 big states. These have been called 16 Mahajanapadas. In this Mahajanapada, Ashmak (Ashmak or Ashvak) was situated on the banks of Godavari River (Andhra Pradesh). Its capital was Potan or Potil. Among the Mahajanapadas, only Ashmaka was situated in South India. The Puranas reveal that the Ashmaka monarchy was established by the Ikshvakuvanshi rulers. Before Mahatma Buddha, Ashmaka was in a continuous struggle with Avanti and during Buddha's time, Avanti won it and included it within its limits. 133
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2003 UPPC: UPPCS (झृ) घुह्गाह History, 2003 UPPCS (झृ) घुघगाह History, (Ejt.) 2004 Explanation- In Vayan Buddhism, the wife of Bodhisattva was known as Tara. From the fifth or sixth century of Christ, the influence of Tantra-Mantras started increasing on Buddhism, as a result of which a new sect called Vayana was born. In these, the method of attaining salvation through mantras and tantric activities was presented. Va» i.e. ‘va»’ is considered as a supernatural element. It has been identified with religion. To achieve this, instead of education, penance etc., emphasis was laid on sexual intercourse, consumption of meat etc. The activities of the scholars are similar to those of the Shatta followers. In this, importance has been given to goddesses like Tara. It has been propounded that Buddha should be worshiped through form, words, touch etc. Ragchaya has been described as the best. The greatest development of the vehicle took place in the 8th century. Vayana paved the way for the decline of Buddhism (in India).
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह. 2012) व्याख: (Uun Nu.- घुघ्घ झजाजी वल्ह. 2012) Explanation – Ajatashatru (Hryaka dynasty) had given the statement 'Bhagavapi Khatriyo Ahamip Khatriyo' i.e. Lord Buddha was also a Kshatriya, I am also a Kshatriya. It is noteworthy that Ajatashatru became the ruler of Magadha by killing his father Bimbasar. He had built a stupa over the remains of Buddha in Rajgriha.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- Satavahanas did not provide state patronage to Jainism. The Satavahana rulers were followers of Vedic religion and supporters of Brahmin religion. During the reign of Rashtrakuta kings (9th century), Jainism spread extensively in South India. In Gujarat and Rajasthan, Jainism remained more popular in the 11th and 12th centuries. Magadha king Ajatashatru and his successor Udayin contributed in their propagation. Jainism also progressed during the period of Nandvansh because they also did not seem to be against Jainism. It is known from the Hathigumpa inscription that Nanda King had taken away the statue of the first 'Jin' from Kalinga. This religion was also propagated during the time of Chandragupta Maurya because according to Jain tradition, he had accepted the discipleship of Jain Acharya Bhadrabahu. At this time Buddhism divided into two sects, Hinayana and Mahayana.

Makyakhaligoshal, the founder of the Aajivaka sect, was the first disciple of Mahavir. But later due to differences of opinions, he left Mahavir and established an independent sect called Aajivak. The 'Ajivaka' 112 sect continued till approximately 1002 AD. Their belief is called fatalism (fatalism), according to which everything in the world is pre-controlled and governed by fate. A man's income has no impact on his life.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी अम. 2015) व्याख्या: (Uun Nu.- घुघ्घ झाजी Am. 2015) Explanation- Magadha ruler Ajatashatru (422-460 BC) had claimed a share in the mortal remains of Buddha on the basis of being a Kshatriya descendant. The eight stupas built on the bone remains of Buddha are as follows – (1) Magadha (Ajatashatru) (2) Vaishali (Lichchavi) (3) Kapilavastu (Shakya) (4) Alakappa (Buliyya) (5) Ramgam (Koliya) (6) A brahna of Vethdwarpa (7) Malla of Pava and (8) Malla of Kushinara.
: गौतम बुद्ध ने अपना पह्ला उपदेश त्र+षिप: : Gautam Buddha gave his first sermon to five Brahmins (Kauninya, Assaji, Vappa, Aanj, Bhadadhanya) in Mrigadava (Sarnath) of Tri + Sipatnam. This sermon is known as the first Dharmachakra Pravartan. This is represented in Buddhist art by the Chakra with the deer in it.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – Vachchedika written by Asanga belongs to the Mahayana sect of Buddhism. The reformist sect of Buddhism is called 'Mahayana'. Mahayana means the best path. In this, special emphasis was given on service and charity. Buddha started being worshiped in the form of an idol. This route was accessible to the general public. Considering its vastness and generosity, its Mahayana name seems completely appropriate. Through this more people could attain salvation. The aim of Mahayana is the welfare of all mankind. It believes in faith and reincarnation. There is also a provision for idol worship. And Buddha's mercy was considered necessary for salvation. The ideal of Mahayana is 'Bodhisattva'. Even after attaining salvation, Bodhisattvas continue to strive for the liberation of other beings. 'The secret of Mahayana's greatness is his selfless service and tolerance.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी अम. 2015) व्याख्या: (Uun Nu.- घघघ झजाजी Am. 2015) Explanation- Most of the disciples of Buddha were in Kosala state and he gave most of the sermons in its capital Shravasti.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2008 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2008 Explanation─Digambara and Shwetambar sects were the two main sects of Jainism. Apart from this, the Yapaniya sect was established by a Shwetambara monk Shri Kalash in 148 AD. Apart from Shwetambar, Digambara and Yapaniya sects, there is mention of Kurchak and Shwetapatta Jain sects in the inscriptions of Kadamba rulers.
Uउण NET-घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–शि: Uun NET-घुझ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – The worshipers of Shiva were called Shaivites and the religion related to them was called Shaivism. This is an ancient religion of India. Its antiquity goes back to ancient history (Indus Valley Civilization), because Marshall has proved the statue depicted on a seal obtained from Mohenjodaro to be an early form of Shiva. Shiva's name Rudra is found in the Vedas. There he was the god of space. Description of Rudra is found in three hymns of Tri + Veda. The saints who propagated Shaivism in South India were called Nayanars. Their total number was 63. In the south, Shaiva Acharya Sundra Mooti was given the title of Tambarantolana (Friend of God).
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ झ्aजी अम. 2012) व्याख्या–: (Uun Nu.- घुझ झाजी अम. 2012) Explanation – 62 philosophical schools or religious sects contemporary to Mahatma Buddha are mentioned in the Brajal Sutta.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह. 2014) व्याख: (Uun Nu.- घघघ झजाजी वल्ह. 2014) Explanation – The trading economy developed a lot during the time of Buddha. Because Buddha had given a lot of encouragement to the traders. Like Buddhists, Jains also encouraged trade. But their inclination towards agriculture remained less.
: जब कोई व्यत्ति संघ में प्रवेश करता है: : When a person enters the Sangha, he becomes colorless (Vevavianit). This sentence/quote is related to Anguttarnikaya. There is mention of 16 Mahajanapadas in Anguttarnikaya and Bhagwati Sutra.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – Anathpindak bought the garden from Prince Jet and gave it for the abode of Buddha. This garden is in Sahet (Shravasti). Shravasti was the capital of Kosala kingdom. During the time of Prasenjit, the Kosala kingdom was at its peak. Apart from Kashi, it also had control over the republics like Shakya of Kapilavastu, Kalam of Kesaputra, Malla of Pava and Kushinara, Koliya of Ramgam, Moriya of Pippalivan etc. According to the Buddhist Anguttarnikaya, he led a group of five kings. Prasenjit was a devotee of Mahatma Buddha and his teachings. Buddha often visited and rested in his capital.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 Explanation- Anga country is mentioned in Pali literature. Its capital was Champa. The area of ​​modern Bhagalpur and Munger was included in the ancient Anga country. During the time of Gautam Buddha, there was a state of constant war in Anga and Magadha districts. For some time, Magadha became a part of Anga country but soon Anga declined and Bimbisara not only took control of Magadha Balik Anga. Anga country is mentioned in Atharvaveda where it has been called a remote region.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History Edt., 2004 Explanation- The chronology of religious great men is as follows - Parshvanath 9th century BC, Mahavir- 599-527 BC, Buddha 563-483, Bhadrabahu- 4th century BC.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- Kalinga ruler Kharavela was a great patron of Jainism. He provided protection to Jain monks, provided them with ample food for their livelihood and built comfortable residences for them. The purpose of the Hathigump article was to preserve the details of similar monk houses built on Udyagiri hill. But despite being a Jain himself, he was tolerant towards other religions. In the thirteenth year of his coronation, Kharavela had cut the hills of Udyagiri and Khandagiri near Bhubaneswar and built caves for the residence of Jain monks. 19 caves were built in Udyagiri and 16 caves in Khandagiri. The paintings engraved in the caves of Rani Gump in Udyagiri and Anant Gump in Khandagiri are of high quality in terms of painting.
