(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह. 2015) व्याख: (Uun Nu.- घघघ झजाजी वल्ह. 2015) Explanation- Buddha had a special attachment to Kushinagar. This city had been his playground in his previous lives also. According to a mention, he had ruled Kushinagar seven times as Chakravata emperor. When Buddha came here for the last time, the Mallas welcomed him very much. On this occasion, the Mallas announced that those who did not attend the reception of Buddha would have to be punished with 500 kashapans.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 PGT: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 PGT 2016 122 Explanation- Among the unorthodox sects that were dominant during the time of Gautam Buddha, the name of Mahvir of Jainism is the most famous. He was not the originator of Jainism but we can call him the originator of the Jain movement of the 6th century BC. He is the most important Indian atheist after Buddha. Tradition calls him the twenty-fourth Tithankar. There have been twenty-three Tithankaras before him. In which the historicity of the twenty-third Tithankar Parshvanath has been proven. Other Tithankaras are as follows - "(1) Tra + Shabha or Adinath, (2) Ajit Nath, (3) Sambhav, (4) Abhinandan, (5) Sumati, (6) Paprabhu, (7) Supashrava, (8) Chandraprabha, (9) Pushpadant, (10) Sheetal, (11) Shreyansh, (12) Vasupujya, (13) Vimal, (14) Anant, (15) Dharma, (16) Sheenit, (17) Kunthu, (18) Aranh, (19) Malil, (20) Muni Subrata, (21) Neminath, (22) Arishtanemi, (23) Parshvanath, (24) Mahavir. Neminath, the twenty-second Tirthankar of Jainism, was related to Krishna. He has been described as a contemporary of Krishna.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2005 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2005 Explanation – Baveru Jataka, Dasharatha Jataka and Shibi Jataka are Buddhist compositions, while Yavana Jataka is an astrological text. 126
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2008 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2008 Explanation-The Ruqmanadei pillar inscription of Maurya Emperor Ashoka is the oldest epigraphic evidence mentioning the birth place of Shakyamuni Buddha. In the 20th year of his consecration, Ashoka went to Luqambani village, built a strong stone wall there and erected a stone pillar. Since Lord Buddha was born there, Luqambani village was declared tax free and only 1/8 share was declared. This information is obtained from Ruqmandei's short column article.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2003 UPPC: UPPCS (झृ) घुघघाह History, 2003 UPPCS (झृ) घुघगाह History, (Edt.) 2004 Explanation- Shiv Puja was widely spread in South India. During the Pallava period, Shaivism was propagated by the Nayanars. The number of Nayanar saints is said to be 63 in which the names of Appar, Tirugnana, Sambandra, Sundramuti, Manikyakavachagar etc. are notable. Their devotional songs were performed simultaneously in the temple. Among these, Appar, whose other name is also found as Tirunobukyakarashu, was a contemporary of Pallava king Mahendra Varman I. He was born in the Bellal family of Thirugmoor. It is said that earlier he used to live the life of a monk while living in a Jain monastery. Later, due to the mercy of Shiva, he was cured of an incurable disease, as a result of which he abandoned Jainism and became a devout Shaiva. Appar worshiped Lord Shiva with ten devotions and propagated it among the common people.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2009 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2009 Explanation─Buddhism was propagated the most in Kosala state. Buddha stayed here for 21 days. Here a very rich merchant named Anathapindaka accepted his discipleship and gave Jetavana Vihar to the Sangha by purchasing it from Prince Jeta for 18 crore gold coins. Kosala king Prasenjit and Avanti king Prasota were contemporaries of Gautam Buddha. Prasenjit accepted the discipleship of Buddha along with his family and built a monastery named Pubbaram for the Sangha. He became the biggest follower of Buddha in Kosala state. Hence, both the statements are correct but the correct explanation of statement A is not R. 128
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- Ashmak (Ashvak) Ashmak Mahajanapada was situated on the banks of Godavari River (Andhra), its capital was Potan or Potil. Among the Mahajanapadas, only Ashmaka was situated in South India. The Puranas reveal that the Ashmaka monarchy was established by the Ikshvakuvanshi rulers. The capital of Mulak was Pratisthan and the capital of Kalinga was Tosali. Avanti Mahajanapada was settled in the region of western and central Malwa. It had two parts - Northern Avanti whose capital was Ujjaini and Southern Avanti whose capital was Mihismati. Vetravati river flowed between the two. Pali scriptures reveal that during the Buddha's time, the capital of Avanti was Ujjaini where its king was Prasota. Ujjaini is identified with the modern Ujjain city of Madhya Pradesh.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी अम. 2014) व्याख्या: (Uun Nu.- घघघ झजाजी Am. 2014) Explanation – Mahatma Buddha reached Shravasti in the 20th year of attaining enlightenment and there made a bandit named Angulimala his disciple. Most of Buddha's disciples were in Kosala state and it was here that he propagated his religion the most. Kosala king Prasenjit was also a disciple of Buddha and said that he was of the same age as Mahatma Buddha. Buddha spent maximum 21 years in Jetavana Vihar of Shravasti. He had made a rule of 4 months of fasting and 8 months of preaching in a year.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2006 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2006 Explanation: According to Esaheli followers Deepavansh and Mahavansh, the third Sangeet of Buddhism took place in Patliputra during the reign of Ashoka. It was presided over by Moggaliputtatisya. After this Sangeet, monks were sent to various countries to propagate Buddhism, whose names are found in the Mahavamsa as follows – Dharma Propagator Countries
: गौतम बुद्ध को हिन्दुओं के वैष्णव सम्प्: : Gautam Buddha is considered to be the incarnation of Lord Vishnu in the Vaishnav sect of Hindus. Buddha is currently considered to be the ninth incarnation among the Dsavatars mentioned in the religion. There will be a final incarnation in the future. Buddha is mentioned in all the major Puranas and all the important Hindu scriptures. In many Puranas, Buddha was considered in the incarnation of Vishnu like - Agnipuran, Bhagwat, Matsya, Garuda Puran, Vishnu, Naradiya Puran.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 Explanation- Shakya Republic gave birth to Buddha's famous disciple Ananda. Ashvaghosha is a contemporary writer of Kanishka. One of whose rhymed poems is Saundranand, which is based on the incident of initiation into Buddhism by Buddha's step brother Anand. Since Buddha was the son of King Shuddhodhan and King Shuddhodhan was the king of the Shakya Republic in North-East Bihar. Kanishka P. from Magadha. He extended his kingdom till Asia but his fame is greater because of his being the patron of Buddhism. His personal religion was Buddhism and he did a lot of work for its promotion and organization. At the behest of Parshva, he organized the fourth Mahasangiti (Mahasabha) of Buddhists in Kashmir and London, in which many scholars participated. The head of this assembly was Vasumitra and Ashvaghosha was the vice-president.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2011 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2011 Explanation – The oldest Jain bronze statues have been found from Chausa. Apart from this, a huge stone statue of Gomateshwara has been found from Shravanabelagola. The world famous Nalanda University was located in Nalanda and statues related to Hindu and Jain sects have been carved from twenty caves in Udyagiri.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 123: UPPCS (झ्र) Ghhgah History, 2002 123 Explanation- Buddha gave his first sermon in Sarnath where five Brahmins became his disciples. After this he started propagating religion. During Vasha Tra + Tu, he used to rest in different cities and in the remaining Tra + Tu, he used to roam from one place to another and propagate his views. He spent his second, third and fourth years in Rajgriha. After leaving the palace, Buddha reached Vaishali, the capital of Lichchhavis. There he spent his fifth rainy season. Buddhism was most propagated in Shravasti, the capital of Kosala state. There Buddha lived twenty-one years. Kosala king Prasenjit also accepted the discipleship of Buddha along with his family and built a monastery named 'Pubbaram' for the Sangha. While living in Shravasti, Buddha succeeded in converting a notorious dacoit named Angulimala, who used to cut off people's fingers and wear their garlands, into his faith. In this way, more followers of Buddha became in Kosala state.
Aेप्araस झ्addप्aूग थम्ू. Exaस. 2012 व्य: अप्रास झड़पुग थम्ू. Exas. 2012 Explanation – 16 Mahajanapadas are mentioned in Anguttarnikaya and Bhagwati Sutra, sixth century BC. There used to be various kings of these districts. In which the capital of Kosala was Shravasti, the king here Prasenjit was a contemporary of Buddha. Kosal Mahajanapada was formed by combining some adjoining districts including modern Faizabad.

अप्रास झड़पुग थम्ू. Exas. 2012 Explanation – Jhalayanaram is situated in Kaushambi. It was built by the famous Shref‰Khalayanaram for the residence of Mahatma Buddha. Emperor Ashoka had built a stupa near Khalakala Ram Ujan.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 125: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 125 Explanation- 'Bhakti' is mentioned in Shwetashwar Upanishad. Vaishnav religion initiated the Bhakti movement in the form of Bhagwat sect. A description of the duties of the four classes is found in Aitareya Brahmana. Sompayee (the man) who gives blessings to the brahmins has been said to be active and to roam around as per his wish (as per Pramal). Shatapatha Brahman gives place to Shudra in Somayajna. It is said in Vridhadaranyaka and Chhandegya Upanishads that everyone is equal in Brahmaloka, hence Chandal is also entitled to get the remains of the yagya. In Shatapatha Brahmana, there is mention of the spread of the Vedic Yagya system towards north-east India. We also know from the Upanishads that King Janak had performed huge Vedic yagyas.
Aेप्araस झ्addप्aूग थम्ू. Exaस. 2012 उ.घ: अप्रास झड़पुग थम्ू. Exas. 2012 U.G. Thummu. Exas 2009 UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2005 Explanation – The founder of Jainism and the first Tithankar was Tri + Shabhadev. Mahavir Swami was the 24th Tithankar. Syadvada (Anekantvad) is included in the philosophical aspects of Jainism. Jainism believes in the soul but does not recognize God. Mahavir Swami added the fifth importance of childhood in Jainism. Jainism has borrowed its spiritual ideas from Sankhya philosophy.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2007 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2007 Explanation - Along with the development of Shaivism, various sects worshiped Shiva in different ways also developed, who worshiped Shiva according to their thoughts, opinions and principles. Gradually, separate classes of worshipers were formed which emerged as independent Shaiva sects. In Shaivagam, the number of such Shaiva sects is stated to be four - (1) Shaiva, (2) Pashupat, (3) Kapalik, (4) Kalamukh. In this, the originator of Pashupat sect was a celibate named Lakulisha who is considered to be an incarnation of Shiva. Kapalikas are mentioned in the play named 'Malti-Madhava'. The followers of Veer Shaiva sect were called 'Jayamt' or 'Jangam'. Kalamukh was also a major Shaiva sect which has been called 'Mahavratadhar'. Vasudev has been called Satvatarsham or Satvat.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी अम. 2014) व्याख्या: (Uun No.- घुघ झाजी Am. 2014) Explanation – Gupta ruler Ramgupta got the statues of Tithankar Chandraprabha and Pushpadatta built.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 Explanation- Prasenajit was a ruler of the same age as Gautam Buddha. Prasenjit was a great ruler of Kosala state. Kosala state extends from Nepal in the north to Sai River in the south and from Panchal in the west to Gandak River in the east. Saryu river divides this district into two parts. The capital of North Kosala was Saket and the capital of South Kosala was Shravasti. Magadha ruler Bimbisara was also a contemporary of Prasenjit, to whom Prasenjit's sister Mahkosala was married and Prasenjit gave the Kashi province as dowry. But Prasenjit had a fight with Ajatashatru and ultimately a compromise was reached between the two and Prasenjit married his daughter Vajira to Ajatashatru.
Uउण NET-घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्त्ब. 2017 व्याख्या: उँ NET-घघ झाजी वल्ट्ब. 2017 Explanation – Kautilya's Arthashastra is an important book for the study of the governance system of the Maurya period. In this, for the first time, it has been suggested to pay salaries to officers in cash. According to this book, top level officials got a salary of 48000 Panas and the lowest level employees got 60 Panas.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History Ejt., 2008 Explanation- Very little respect has been shown towards Buddhists in Kautilya's Arthashastra. Kautilya has clearly discouraged people from taking up sannyasa without making arrangements for the support of their families.
Uउण NET-घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–नह: Uun NET-घुझ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – Nahapan was the most famous ruler of the Kshahrata dynasty. Its coins have been found from the area from Ajmer to Nashik. These are of silver or copper. Coins are of certain standard. During his time the exchange rate of gold and silver coins was 1:35. In an article from Nashik, the value of 70 thousand Kashapanas was given in 2000 gold coins. On coins he bears the title of 'Rajand'. An inscription of Amatya Aryamand of Nahapan is found from Juvar (Poona).
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History Astt., 2008 Explanation – Puhar port is situated at the mouth of Kaveri. Initially, Chola ruler Karikala protected the port of Puhar on the banks of Kaveri by building a fort. He employed the soldiers of Eshal (Lanka) in this work. Puhar is described as a busy port in Tamil literature of the first century AD. A very vivid description of Puhar is found in the Tamil text Patitnappalai.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2006 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2006 Explanation: Maurya Emperor Ashoka, 273 BC. Around 1500 BC, the king of Magadha sat on the throne. Everywhere in his inscriptions he has been addressed with the titles of 'Devanampriya', 'Priyadshaa' and 'Raja' etc. Among Ashoka's successors, Dashrath also held the title of 'Devanampriya' like Ashoka.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2005 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2005 Explanation – Tondi (modern Pouni) was an important port for establishing trade relations between India and the Roman Empire. Whose important information has been given by the author of Periplus (75AD). Since in the above question option, only Cheros ruled in the west of South India. Therefore the answer will be Cher.
Uउण NET-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–: Uun NET-घुघ्घ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – After Huvishka, Kanishka II (Kanishka- Samvatd 62 to 67) became the king. He is mentioned in Ara stone inscription 41. He was the son of Vasishka. It appears that he ruled jointly with Huvishka for some time. In the stone inscription 41 of Arrah, Maharaj had adopted the titles of 'Rajadhiraj', 'Devputra' and 'Kaiser' (Caesar) etc. in imitation of the then Roman kings. Which is mentioned in the stone inscription of Ara.

Uun NET-घुघ्घ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – Although the Yavana kings introduced gold coins in North-West India, the credit for making them prevalent regularly and completely can be given to the Kushan kings. The figures of various gods and goddesses and their names in Greek are engraved on the reverse side of the coin of the Kushan ruler Huvishka. In Indian deities, apart from Buddha and Shiva, Vishnu, Mahasen, Kumar, Vishakh, Uma etc. are also mentioned. Uma is shown with a lotus or prosperity in her hand.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – Kushan ruler Kanishka has obtained majority of gold and copper coins from various places in Sikkim, North-Western Province, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Bengal and Orissa. The gold coin is equal in weight to Roman coins (about 124 pounds). On the reverse side of some coins of Kanishka, the figure of four-armed Shiva and Isen (Shiva) are inscribed in Greek. He has Trishul, Damru and Kakush in his hand. On some coins, there is a statue of Buddha in a standing posture with a halo and below it 'Voje' (Buddha) himself in Greek script and some such copper coins have been found on which the figure of a king in a sitting posture is depicted. The weight of four of these coins is 68 pounds. Gardner has mentioned some bronze coins of Kanishka. On their main part, the standing figure of the king and his Greek title are inscribed. There are figures of Greek gods and goddesses on the back side. 180
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2005 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2005 Explanation – Detailed information about the Kalag war and its results is obtained from the thirteenth inscription of Ashoka. After the victory, two subordinate administrative centers were established in Kalag. The ancient kingdom of Kalinga was located in present-day southern Orissa. It is clear from this that this war was very fierce in which incidents of horrific bloodshed and massacre took place. Ultimately Ashoka was successful in conquering this state and annexing it to his empire. Unfortunately, we do not know the name of the ruler of Kalinga from any evidence. In the thirteenth inscription, the terrible consequences of this war have been mentioned in this way – in this, one lakh 50 thousand people were taken captive and exiled, one lakh people were murdered and many times more than this died. The Brahmins, Shramanas and householders who did not take part in the war suffered greatly due to the killing of their relatives. The emperor had seen this massive massacre with his own eyes.

Ilango Adigal was the younger brother of the Chera ruler Senguttuvan. The plot is based on a popular story. ''Kovalan, son of a famous rich businessman of Puhar (Kaveripatnam) is married to Kannagi, a businessman's daughter. The married life of both of them passes happily for a few days. One day, at a function of Rajprasad, Kovalan meets a dancer named Madhavi. The dancer fascinates Kovalan with her beauty and expressions, and he, trapped in her love, not only forgets his beloved Kannagi and her sweet love, but also sacrifices his entire wealth for the false love of Madhavi. When Kovalan has nothing left, he realizes his mistake and comes back to his beloved Kannagi.

On the basis of Kanishka's coins and Peshawar inscription, it seems that he converted to Buddhism in the initial years of his rule. He expressed his devotion towards this religion by building the famous Chaitya in Purushapur, Peshawar. फेंसांग had visited Kanishka Vihar located in Peshawar. Kanishka provided royal patronage to the Mahayana branch of Buddhism and propagated it in Central Asia and China. 181

UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – Chandragupta's well-organized administrative system was based on a strong financial base, the government had strict control over all the economic activities of the empire. Special attention was paid to the progress of agriculture and official land was made agricultural. Both the state and the farmer had rights over the land. The main officer who managed the state land was 'Sitadhyaksha', who got the farming done with the help of ten workers and servants. Some government land was given to farmers for farming. The main source of income of the state was land tax on the principle: 1/6 heta of the produce. The income received from government land is called 'Sita'. Such people used to give a 'part' of their produce to the king as tax. Land tax was called Bhag.

It is said that 449 poets had presented their works before it for acceptance and all of them got permission from the administration. Nakyakirar's name is mentioned as its president. Among the excellent works related to the third Sangam, Nedunalvadai, Kurunthauke Nattinai, Enkurunnuru, Padittuppat, Nutrambatha, Paripadala, Vaari, Parisai, and Sitrisai are notable. UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 Explanation- Nahapan was the ruler of Kshahraat dynasty. Its coins have been found from the area from Ajmer to Nashik. They are of silver and copper and the exchange ratio of gold and copper was 1:35. On coins he bears the title of 'Rajand'. An inscription of Amatya Aryamand of Nahapan is found from Junnar (Poona). The inscriptions of his son-in-law Tra+Shabhaddat (Ushavdat) have been found in Nashik and Kalax (Poona). During the time of Tra + Shabhadatta Nahapana, he was the governor of his southern provinces - Govardhan (Nashik) and Mamalla (Puna). It is known from a cave inscription of Nashik that when the people of Uttambhadra caste of Rajasthan were surrounded by the Malavas, Tra + Shabhadatta went there to protect them. He defeated the Malavas badly and after this he sacrificed his life in Pushkartirtha. From this it seems that he donated in Pushkar Teerth of Rajputana. From this it seems that the Pushkar pilgrimage (Ajmer) area of ​​Rajputana was also influenced by Nahapan.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृहगाह History, 2002 Explanation- Tagar was not a Sangam era port whereas Arikamedu, Uraiyur and Korkai were Sangam era ports. From the excavation at Arikamedu, (Pindicherry), fragments of Roman coins, glass cut gems, beads and utensils have been recovered. One bead has a portrait of the Roman emperor Augustus on its back. This shows that there was a deep trade relationship between India and Rome in the first two centuries AD. Arikamedu was a famous trading center where trade goods were collected from different parts of the country and sent to Rome from here. India also benefited from trade relations with Rome. As long as trade relations with Rome continued, the Tamil kingdoms of the south remained prosperous. But when trade declined, these states also began to decline. The unknown author of 'Periplus' (1st century AD) presents details of close trade relations between India and Rome. He mentions the rich ports of the west coast like Naura, Mushiri, Tondi Leesand.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2003 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2003 Explanation- In Sangam literature, Kaveripatnam was related to Cholas. The capital of the Chola dynasty was initially Uraiyur, later it was shifted to Puhar which came to be known as Kaveripatnam. Kaveripatnam was a prosperous port during this period. From where big ships loaded with goods used to come to foreign countries. The poet of Pattinappalai has presented a very detailed and lively description of the progress of industry and trade in the areas of Kaveripatnam. Encouraged conversion of forests into agricultural land and increased the number of ponds for irrigation. It was natural that Hena became prosperous in Karikala's kingdom due to these efforts. For this reason he ruled happily for a long time.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2003 PGT: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2003 PGT History, 2010 Explanation- Megasthenes, the messenger of Greek ruler Seleucus, came to the court of Maurya ruler Chandragupta Maurya. Megasthenes has described the then Indian society in his book 'Indaka'. Megasthenes' description shows that peace and prosperity prevailed in the Maurya era. The people were completely self-reliant. And the land was very productive. He was excellent in public morals and lived a life of simplicity. Indians were courageous, brave and truthful. His attire was simple. Wheat and barley were the main grains. According to Megasthenes there were seven classes in the society. Philosopher, farmer, hunter, cattle herder, businessman, craftsman, warrior, inspector and minister. Megasthenes has praised the Brahmin sages. According to him, Indians worshiped the Greek gods Dionysus and Hercules. Actually, it means worship of Shiva and Krishna.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 Explanation- The word Rudradamak found in the inscriptions of Western India means the dynasty run by the Shaka king. The inscriptions of the Satavahana kings give us information about their relations with the Shakas. Apart from the inscriptions, a large number of coins of Shaka kings have been found from large parts of western and northern India. Kanishka's writings show that some Shaka-Kshatrapas and Mahakshatrapas ruled some parts of the country under his subordination. There are mentions of Shakas here and there in Indian literature also. In Ramayana and Mahabharata, Shakas have been mentioned along with foreign races like Yavana, Pahlva etc. Katyayana and Patanjali were also familiar with the Shakas. In Manusmriti we find its mention along with Parad Dravina Pahlva etc. Castes like Shaka, Murund, Yavana etc. have also been mentioned in the Puranas.

Bhadrabahu's Kalpasutra and Hemchandra's Parishishtaparvan are Jain texts. From this, we know about some events in the life of Chandragupta Maurya. Among the Brahmin literature, Puranas, Kautilya's Arthashastra, Visakhadutta's Mudrarakshas drama etc. are prominent. From which all the necessary information related to the personality and creation of the Maurya Emperor is obtained.

Ashoka's national king Tushasp of Yavana caste had constructed a dam on that lake. This dam broke for the first time during the reign of Shakamahakshatrapa Rudradaman (130-150 AD). Which he had rebuilt after spending a lot of money under the direction of his governor Suvisakh. Junagadh inscription shows that during the reign of Skandagupta, the dam of the historical Sudrashan Lake broke due to heavy rains. For a moment, that beautiful lake became Sudrashan i.e. a frightening sight for the entire world. Due to this the people started suffering a lot. To solve this problem, Chakrapalit, son of the governor of Saurashtra province, Parnadatta, who was the mayor of Girnar city, within two months spent a lot of money and got the dam of that lake rebuilt by inlaying stones. According to the article, this dam was a hundred hands long and sixty eight hands wide. Due to this the people breathed a sigh of happiness and Sudrashan Lake became stable in eternal form.

Names of five provinces are found in his inscription. In economics, 'Sanstha' has come for intelligence. The intelligence department was kept under a separate Amatya who was called 'Mahamatyapasarp'. Spies were called 'mysterious men' in economics. Those men were appointed in this department whose purity of character and loyalty were tested in every way. There was a web of spies spread throughout the society. He used to travel around in various disguises and used to inform the emperor about his daily activities. There is mention of two types of spies in the Arthashastra - 'Sanstha' i.e. those who stay at one place and 'Sanchara' i.e. men who travel from place to place. Apart from men, clever women also used to do spies. Arthashastra shows that prostitutes were also appointed to the posts of spies.

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 Explanation- Gautam Dharmasutra is considered to be the oldest among the sutras. Gautama has prescribed the duties of all the monks. Gautam has described the social prestige of Brahma as supreme. The main duty of the king (Kshatriya) was war and governance. Vaishya people earned their living through agriculture, animal husbandry and commerce. The condition of Shudras was pathetic. The social status of Vaishyas was gradually coming closer to that of Shudras. First of all, Gautam has called Varta (agriculture, animal husbandry, commerce) as the general profession of Shudra caste. Varnas became rigid and turned into castes, the basis of which was birth rather than work. Inter caste marriage and eating habits were clearly banned. Shudras were considered the most inferior and powerless class of the society. Along with the caste system, the ashram system was created for the purpose of regularizing the life of the individual.

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 207: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 207 Explanation- Many socio-economic historians have expressed their views on the emergence and development of feudalism in the modern era. But the word feudal has been mentioned in Kautilya's Arthashastra in the sense of 'independent neighbour'. For the first time Ashvaghosha (1st century) has used this word for Jagirdar in Buddhacharita. From the Gupta period the word Samant started being used generally in this sense. The germination of feudalism took place during the Shaka-Kushana period and by the Rajput period it became completely prevalent in the society. The Jain text 'Kalakacharya' shows that the Shakd emperor was called 'Shahanushihi' and there were many feudal lords (shihi) under his subordination. The title of 'Rajadhiraja' of the Kushan emperors is also indicative of the feudal system. The titles of 'Mahkshatrapa' and 'Kshatrapa' were prevalent among the Shaka rulers of Western India. Later, the Gupta emperors followed him and adopted the title of 'Maharajadhiraj'. In this way, feudalism became completely established in the political field during the Gupta period and thereafter.

Chyavan married Sukanya, Shyavasya married Rathveeti, Agastya married Lopamudra etc. Kshatriya girls. Under Pratiloma Vivah, a girl from a higher caste was married to a man from a lower caste. This type of marriage is considered condemnable.

Apart from this, he needed money to expand his empire in Central Asia. He could easily get money in India. Therefore, to collect wealth, Mahmud launched several attacks on India one after the other.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- In 731 AD, the Arabs established the first city on the banks of river Indus at Mahpuja and after that the second city was established at Mansoora. Dahir himself got frightened by his attack and did not send any army to face him in Dewal. In this way, without any resistance, Muhammad got the southern part of Sindh. Muhammad Habib has termed these changes as an urban revolution. According to him, Tuka uprooted the age-old caste and ideological restrictions on industrial and social forces. In this way, Habib considers the Tuka conquest of North India as the revolution of the urban artisans of India.

There is no information available from its writings regarding the origin of this dynasty. Parvata writers establish its relation with the Chalukya dynasty of Badmi and describe it as a descendant of the younger brother of Vikramaditya II, whose name is unknown but whose title was 'Bhima Parakram'. It was the name of the rulers of Chalukya dynasty north of Kalyani that its ancestors used to rule in Ayodhya. It is mentioned in the Kaithom inscription of Vikramaditya VI that 59 Chalukya kings ruled in Ayodhya. In the absence of any clear evidence, we can accept it as a possible hypothesis.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- Chinese travelers used to call India as 'Yind-Tu' or Tiyin Tu'. Impressed by the simplicity and practicality of Buddhism, many Chinese travelers traveled to India to buy copies of Buddhist texts and to visit sacred Buddhist places. Among these, the names of Pahiyan, £ensang and Itisag are most famous. Pahiyan came here in the fourth century and traveled to various places. At this time Chandragupta Ghh was ruling. In his travelogue, he has drawn a beautiful picture of the society and culture of the Gupta period. Mahatsang came to India during the reign of Harshavardhana and has described the political and cultural condition of India during Harshavardhana's time. Itisag came to India in the seventh century (671 AD). In his travelogue he has described Nalanda University.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – Manusmriti is the most ancient and authentic among the Smritis. It was composed around the Shunga period (2nd century BC). Most of the memories have been written in this context. Evidence of Manusmriti has been given in Yajnavalkya Smriti, Smritis of Vishnu, Narad, Brihaspati etc. All these are creations of the Gupta period (fifth century AD). Over time, important commentaries were written on the memories of Manu, Yajnavalkya etc. Famous commentators of Manusmriti are Medhatithi, Govind Raj and Kullukbhatta and commentators of Yajnavalkya Smriti are Vishvaroop, Vijnaneshwar and Aparak etc. Aparak was the famous Shilaharvanshi ruler of Konkar. The usefulness of memories is important from the point of view of study of Indian history. It comprehensively discusses the governance, religion, social, economic, traditions, ethics, etc. of its time.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 Explanation- Vakyapati II (973-995) was a Parmar ruler. He was also called Munj. He had built Munjsagar Tadg in his capital Dhara. The first independent and powerful king of the Parmar dynasty was Siyak or Harsha. There was a conflict with the Rashtrakutas and after defeating Khotig, Siyak looted vast wealth. Started during the time of Vakyapati Munj. He defeated the kings of Tripuri, Lat (Gujarat), Karnataka, Chola and Kerala in the war. His most famous victory was over the Chalukya king Tailapa II of Kalyani. But later in another encounter Tailap also emerged victorious. Bhoj was the most popular king of this dynasty. According to the Udyapur Prashasti, he fought with many Indian kings, especially Indnath of Chedi, the first Joggal of Gujarat and Bhima, the kings of Lat and Kanat, Gurjara and Turukya. To avenge the death of his uncle (Vakdapati Manuj), he defeated the Chalukya king Vikramaditya IV of Kalyani.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – A special class emerged in the early medieval society which is called 'feudal'. This is said to be the most powerful class of the society. The weakness of the central power created a class of influential persons in the society on whom the burden of local security fell. The land and village grants given by the then rulers also had a major contribution in the development of feudalism. R.S. Sharma is of the opinion that feudalism in India arose due to the kings giving land and village grants to the Brahmins and administrative and military officials. The unequal distribution of land and power due to excessive land grants led to the emergence of new classes in the society. For whom the administrators of the early medieval period tried to find a place in the traditional caste system. In order to maintain purity in the society, the rules regarding marriage, food habits and untouchability were made very strict.

Despite slight differences, the tendency of all of them kept getting pulled towards Sagun Bhakti. All of them rejected the complete unity of Brahma and the soul and propagated the belief that after worldly birth the unification of the soul with Brahma ends. Due to the efforts of Vaishnavas, Bhagavad Gita got importance and prestige, with the establishment of incarnationism, worship of incarnations and exaltation of brahmins etc. Vallabhacharya especially emphasized on worshiping the idol of God. Vallabhacharya was the main saint of Krishna Bhakti branch. He established 'Pushit Marg' and developed Shuddvaita. Vallabhacharya never took up sannyasa and used to give the message of salvation while living a family life.

The specialty of Kailash temple is that to build it, not only was the mountain dug downwards, but the craftsmen started carving the rock from the top part. In this way all the parts of the temple were carved from top to bottom.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 Explanation- The 'Agnikund theory' of the origin of Rajputs is mentioned in Chandrabardai's book 'Prithvirajraso'. Vashi‰ Muni performed a yagya on Mount Abu from which four heroes were born and after whom Chahamana, Chalukya, Parmar and Pratihar dynasties were established. It seems that the origin of Rajputs has been explained by Agnikund in 'Prithvirajraso' for the purpose of incorporating these foreign castes into the Indian society through Shuddha. According to this story, 'When Parashurama destroyed the Kshatriyas, there was a shortage of rulers. The atrocities of Mlechchas and Rakshasas increased. The earth woke up distressed. Therefore, to end the troubles of the earth, Vashi performed yagya on Mount Abu. It is clearly mentioned from this story that the Indian caste systems had given place to the foreign castes under the Indian caste system through Shuddha.

Many palaces and temples were built here, of which Saraswati temple was the most prominent. He himself was a scholar. And his title was Kaviraj. UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झ्र) घृह्गाह History, 2001 Explanation- Saint Kumaril Bhatt of South India founded Purva Mimamsa philosophy. Upanishads and Vedanta are called Uttaramimansa because in them we find discussion of knowledge instead of rituals. The pioneer of Purvamimamsa is Jaimini. Whose book 'Mimamsa Sutra' is the sutra of this philosophy. Kumaril Bhatt and Prabhakar are his other philosophers in whose name two independent schools of Mimamsa came into existence. The main subject of Mimamsa has been said to be religion, according to which Vedas are the origin of religion.

Dhruvasena, the ruler of Balbhi, is called the son-in-law of Hrsha by Hiuen Tsang (Yuwan Tsang). In 637 AD, Huensang went to Nalanda University. The Vice Chancellor here was Acharya Shilabhadra. He lived in Nalanda for about one and a half years and studied Yogashastra. After this, he went to Kachi, the capital of Pallavas, via Bengal, Orissa, Dhanyakatta (on the banks of river Krishna).

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – Shiva worship was widely spread in South India. During the time of dynasties like Chalukya, Rashtkut, Pallava, Chola etc. who ruled in the South, Shaivism progressed and many temples and statues of Shiva were built. During the Pallava period, Shaivism was propagated by the Nayanars. The number of Nayanar saints is said to be 63, among which the names of Appar Tirugnana, Samband, Sundramooti Manikyakavachagar etc. are notable. Their devotional songs have been compiled together in 'Devaram', among them Appar, whose other name is Tirunanukyakarashu, was a contemporary of Pallava king Mahendravarman I. He was born in a Vellala family of Thirugmoor.
Uउण NET-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–: Uun NET-घुघ्घ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – Buddhist texts mention three sons of Udayin – (a) Aniddha (अ) Mundaka and Nagadsaka. The last king Nagadsaka was somewhat famous. In the Puranas he has been called 'spectator'. The historicity of the audience is also proved in Mahakavi Bhas's famous play Swapnavasavadta. These three rulers were very weak and luxurious. Hence the governance system became weak. Conspiracies and murders started happening all around.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 Explanation- Except Dravidian scripts, all other scripts have originated from Brahmi script. This script was fully developed in the Maurya era. Later, during the Gupta period, it was called 'Gupta Brahma' and its expansion extended to far South-East Asia and Central Asia. A special script, Siddhamatrika or low-angled script, was developed from the eastern sub-branch of the western branch of this Gupta Brahma. The time of its development is considered to be around 6th century. Later, the Gupta Brahma script developed into three major scripts (a) Sharada, (अ) Kutila, (म) Nagari scripts. These three scripts are the mother of modern North Indian scripts.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 280: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 280 Explanation- We get the history of Parmar dynasty on the basis of inscriptions, literature and foreign descriptions. The first record of this dynasty is the Hasal inscription of Siyak II (948 AD). From which the early history of Parmar dynasty is known. Other inscriptions include the Ujjain inscription of Vakapatimanuj (980 AD), the inscriptions of Bhoj's Banswad and Betma, the Udyapur inscription of the time of Udayaditya, the Nagpur inscription of Lakshmandev, which is inscribed on the T of a stone slab of the Neelkantheshwar temple of a place called Udyapur near Bhilsa. This is the main means of knowing the names of the rulers of Parmar dynasty and their achievements. This type of description is not found anywhere else. From this description it is known that the ruler of Parmar dynasty, Naravarman had assumed the title of 'Nirvana Narayan'.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – The first notable name is the name of Pagupta 'Parmal', the author of 'Navsahsacharita', considered to be the first epic of Sanskrit literature, who used to reside in the royal court of Paramara dynasty ruler Munj (973-995 AD). In this epic, he has described the events of the life of Munj and his brother Sindhuraj. Following the example of Kalidas, this poem has also been composed in Vaidabha style. The language is ornamental and informative. Whereas Somdev had composed Kathasaritsagara. This book was composed by Somdev for the entertainment of Suryavati, the queen of Kashmir King Anant.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 277: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 277 Explanation- Chamundarai, the minister of Ganga king Rajamall IV, had installed a huge statue of Gomateshwara, the son of the first Tithankara, at Shravanabelagola in Mysore. This statue is 17 meters high. Chamundarai had installed the statue of Gomateshwara in the Vibhava year of 6th century on Chaitra Shukyal Panchami at midnight on March 13, 981 AD. This idol is standing in Kayotsarga posture, carved from all sides from head to thighs. This statue has been carved out of rock from knees to feet. The remaining rock has been given the shape of a bobby with snakes coming out of it. Madhavi's creeper is drawn on his hands. Daily worship is only for the feet. Mastakabhishek is done after a fixed period of time. This happens in a certain period after ten to fifteen years. Many sages, priests and pilgrims participate in it. There is also a celebration of 'hen' here. This is the world's largest rock-cut statue made on Vindhyagiri mountain.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झ्र) घृह्गाह History, 2002 Explanation- 'Ramcharit' is a famous poem written by Sandhyakar Nandi. It describes the history of Pal ruler Rampal and Parvata Pal rulers. After Harsh's contemporary Shashank, the power of Bengal was consolidated under the leadership of Pala dynasty and soon they started being counted among the major powers of North India. The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala, a follower of Buddhism. The feudal lords of Bengal were impressed by Gopal's ability to end the political strife and turmoil of Bengal and chose him as their ruler. These feudal lords sacrificed their personal interests for the welfare of the state. According to Tibetan historian Taranath, Gopal was born in a Kshatriya family of Pundvardhan (Bogra district). He expanded the state through war and also provided organization to the state.

UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- Patanjali was the priest of Pushyamitra Sunga. In his Mahabhashya there is mention of Yavana invasion. In which it is told that the Yavanas had crushed Saket and Madhyamika. Malvikaginamitra is the play of great poet Kalidasa. From this we get knowledge of the political activities of the Sunga period. It is revealed that Pushyamitra's son Agnimitra was the governor of Vidisha and he had conquered Vidharbha and annexed it to his kingdom. Kalidasa also mentions the Yavana invasion. According to which Agnimitra's son Vasumitra had defeated the Yavanas on the right bank of the Indus river. Matsya, Vayu and Brahmand are especially noteworthy in the Puranas. The Puranas reveal that Pushyamitra was the founder of the Sunga dynasty. Pajitra considers only the details of Matsya Purana as authentic. According to them, Pushyamitra ruled for 36 years.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – Pravarasena I (275-335 AD) was the only ruler of the Vakataka dynasty who held the title of emperor. This indicates his power and prestige. He was a conquering ruler who expanded his kingdom in all directions. Pravara Sen I was a devout Brahmin, who, apart from four Ashvamedha and one Vajpeya Yagya, also performed many other Vedic Yagyas. Altekar estimates that he would have performed each yagya in close proximity to a military campaign. In the first campaign he conquered the eastern and north-eastern parts of the central province. The second military campaign took place in the south. In that he conquered southern Berar and northern Andhra Pradesh. In his remaining campaigns, Pravarasena conquered the Shakas of Gujarat and Kathiawar. In this way, as a result of his victories, Pravarasena created a huge empire for himself.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation: Around the fourth century AD, the practice of Sati started gaining popularity. Writers like Vatsyayana, Bhasava, Kalidas and Shudraka have mentioned it. The first documentary evidence of the practice of Sati is from the Gupta period. The Eran inscription of 510 AD reveals that Gupta king Bhanugupta's friend Goparaj was killed while fighting against the Huns and his wife was burnt to death in the fire. But the great poet Banabhatta opposed it and called it a costly and foolish act which has no meaning. This is suicide and the woman who follows it is called Narak Gamini Heti. Medhatithi considers it as suicide and says that it is prohibited for women. Devbhatta is of the opinion that Sati Heena is more heinous than the celibacy of a widow.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2011 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2011 Explanation – In the system of Yajnavalkya, the wife's position is first in the succession order of a sonless deceased. Vijnaneshwar greatly expanded its scope and included under it the property acquired by inheritance, purchase, partition, husbandry and acquisition. (Renewable portfolio acquisition). In this way, almost every type of property belonging to a woman was included under 'Stree Dhan'.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- 'Aparajitprichha' written by Bhattbhuvandev is the book of Vastushastra. It was composed in the 12th century. In this chapter, houses of different sizes are mentioned for the categories of feudal lords including Mahamandaleshwar, Mandalika, Mahasamanta and Laghu Samanta. There are clear indications in contemporary texts that such various positions were not limited to Kshatriyas only. At the time of land acquisition and division, a new educated class (Kayastha) emerged. The transformation of Shudras into farmers and the decline in the status of Vaishyas to Shudra level also led to significant changes in the varna system, so much so that in the new Brahmin system established in Bengal and South India, provision was made mainly for Brahmins and Shudras only. The most astonishing change of this era was the multiplication of castes which affected all Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. 278

The ancient name of Kalax was Baluraka. It presents an excellent example of Satavahana architecture of 100 AD (1st century AD). There is no other presence in cave temples more developed over time, fully decorated and beautiful. The length of the Kalax group is 124 feet 3 inches and width is 45 feet 6 inches. The height of the arched roof from the floor is 45 feet. There is a row of 37 pillars between the central and side parts.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2007 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2007 Explanation – The author of 'Kapur Manjari', Rajshekhar Pratihar was the guru of ruler Mahendrapal I. Rajashekhar has called Mahendrapala I as 'Fearless King' and 'Fearless Narendra'. While under the patronage of Mahendrapala I, Rajshekhar composed the play 'Kapur Manjari' (Prakrat language) and the plays 'Vidvasalbhanjika', 'Bal Ramayana', 'Bal Bharat' (Prachanda Pandava) in Sanskrit and poetry collections named 'Kavya Mimansa', 'Bhuvankosh' and 'Harvilas'. Rajashekhar also lived during the time of Mahendrapal I's successor Mahipal I and gave Mahipal I the epithet of Raghukulmuktamani and Maharajadhiraja of Ayavarta.
Uउण NET-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–: Uun NET-घुघ्घ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – Shatapatha Brahmana, 1089 Kashmir manuscript is the first manuscript written on paper.

Uउण NET-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी व्aह. 2017 व्याख्या–: Uun NET-घघ्घ झजाजी वाह. 2017 Explanation – It belonged to the Chalukya dynasty of Kalyani whose ancestors ruled Ayodhya. In the 'Kathom' article of the ruler of this dynasty, Vikramaditya श‰, it is said that 59 Chalukya kings ruled in Ayodhya, then they went to the south. Apart from this, the writings in Kavar language of the kings of this dynasty and their feudal lords throw light on the then history. In these evidences, he has been described as a descendant of the Chalukyas of Vatapi and a native of Ayodhya.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- 'Ashwamedha Parakram:' is based on Samudra Gupta's coin. On their face there is a picture of a horse tied in Yagya Yoop and the inscription that Rajadhiraj conquers the heaven by conquering the earth and performing the ritual of Ashwamedha Yagya. (राजधिराजो पर्थिविजित्य दिव जयत्या ग्रहीतवाजिमेध:) is engraved. On the reverse side, along with the figure of Rajmahishi (Dattadevi), Ashwamedha Parakram is inscribed. The Puranas reveal that Pravarasena I had performed four Ashwamedha Yagya. Altekar says that Pravarasena would have performed each yagya at the proximity of a military campaign. Pravarasena I was a devout Brahmin who performed four Ashwamedha Yagyas and one Vajpayee Yagyam apart from many other Vedic Yagyas. The founder of the Chalukya dynasty of Badmi was a person named Pulakeshin I. He held titles like Satyashray and Ranvikram and he performed Vedic Yagyas like Ashwamedha Bajpai etc. and he was knowledgeable of Manusmriti, Itihas, Purana, Ramayana, Mahabharata etc.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2005 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2005 Explanation – Tondaiman considers himself to be originated from Vishnu. The Chera kingdom was spread in the area of ​​Western Tamilakam i.e. modern North Travancore, Cochin and South Malabar. The capital of Cheras was Wajij. The Chola kingdom was located on the Coromandel Coast in South India, its capital was Tanjore. The Pandya kingdom was located in the far south, its capital was Madura, where three Sangams were held.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2002 Explanation- We know the history of Chalukya dynasty of Gujarat mainly from the texts of Jain writers. These writers resided in the Rajya Sabha of the Chalukya rulers. Among these texts, Dvashraya Kavya, Merutungakrat, Prabandha Chintamani, Someneshwarakrat Kitikaumudi Jaisingh Suri Krat Kumar Pal Charit etc. can be mentioned. By studying which we get details of the political and cultural achievements of the rulers of this dynasty. Apart from Indian literature, we get information about the conflict between Tuka and Chalukyas from the descriptions of Muslim writers like Algada, Ibt-ul-Atahar, Hasan Nizami etc. After the rule of Chalukya or Solanki ruler Kumarpal, Ajay Pal became the ruler, who ruled from 1172-76 AD. There was a Shaiva reaction during his period. According to Jain beliefs, he killed Jain monks and demolished Jain temples. One of his servants stabbed him to death.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2006 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2006 Explanation: Dravidian style temples were completely different from North-Indian temples. Southern influence is visible in some North Indian temples. For example, the famous Baital Deul temple of Bhubaneswar (Orissa) has the pinnacle of Gopuram style (Dravidian style). Among the temples of Orissa, the Elgaraj Temple (1000 AD) located at Bhubaneswar is considered to be a perfect example of Hindu temple architecture. The Lingaraja Temple, the Jagvath Temple and the Rajarani Temple are examples of Nagara style. The peak (ganda) of the Baital Deul temple rises for some distance above the level of other temples of Orissa. After that, the roof level rises. It has the shape of a cube. There are three pillars on the upper floor. Its walls have multi-decorated panels on the front and back. It is a specialty of the temples of South India.
Uउण NET-घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्त्ब. 2017 व्याख्या: उँ NET-घघ झाजी वल्ट्ब. 2017 Explanation – Chauhan dynasty ruler Viharaja IV established a Sanskrit educational institution named 'Saraswati Temple' in Ajmer, and also constructed Avasagar Lake.
उँ NET-घघ झाजी वल्ट्ब. 2017 Explanation – Borobudur is a Mahayana Buddhist monastery located in Indonesia. It was constructed by the rulers of Shailendra dynasty in the 9th century. 273
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2001 Explanation- Drona was a unit of measuring grains. Apart from this, there were weights for measuring grain, Prastha, Adak, and Khari. Both the state and the farmer had rights over the land. The main officer who managed the state land was 'Sitadhyaksha' who got the farming done with the help of tenants, workers and servants. Some government land was given to farmers for farming. The main source of income of the state was land tax. This principle was 1/6 of the produce, but in practice it was increased somewhat according to the economic situation. Arthashastra and some Greek evidences show that during the Maurya period, people had to pay a tax of up to 25 gyas on agricultural income. By such land was meant government land.

UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2001 Explanation- Shravasti was the capital of Kosala state, it was the main state of North-East India. Even before Mahatma Buddha, a king named Kansa had conquered the Kashi state. In Jataka's verses, Kṛṣṇa is said to be 'Baran Sighāhen' i.e. the one who has control over Banaras. Kamsa was succeeded by Mahakosala. During this time Kosal had complete control over Kashi. Evidence of coins issued by Shravasti has been found. Kaushambi was the capital of Vatsa Mahajanapada. The modern Allahabad and Band districts used to form Vatsa 276 Mahajanapada in ancient times. King Nichakshu of Hastinapur made Kaushambi his capital after Hastinapur was washed away by the flow of Ganga. During the Buddha's time, the Paurava dynasty ruled here whose ruler was Udyan. Present Varanasi and its surrounding area was Kashi Mahajanapada in ancient times. The city of Varanasi, surrounded by Varuna in the north and Asi rivers in the south, was the capital of Kashi Mahajanapada. Evidence of coins issued by all these cities has been found.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – Both Ballalsen and Dharampal were rulers. Ballalsen became the ruler of the Sen dynasty of Bengal around 1159 AD. After ending the remaining power of the Pala dynasty of Bengal, he assumed the title of Gaudeshwar. His other titles were – Parambhattarak, Maharajdhiraj, Parameshwar, Paramaheshwar, Nishank Shankar etc. Ballal Sen himself was a scholar and a patron of scholars, he had composed a book named Dansagar and had started the composition of a book called 'Adbhut Sagar' but could not complete it. After Gopal, the founder of Pala dynasty, his son Dharampal became the ruler. Dharmapala was an ardent Buddhist. In his writings it has been called 'the ultimate gift'. He established the famous monasteries at Vikramshila and Sompuri (Pahadpur). The famous Buddhist writer Hribhadra resided in his palace. According to Ram Rai, he had established 50 religious schools. But as a king he did not have religious intolerance and fanaticism.
सही सुमेल इस प्रकार है : (a) बुद्धगुप्त: The correct combination is as follows: (a) Buddhagupta - Paramdaivat (m) Kumaragupta - Parambhagwat (m) Pravarsen Ghh - Paramamaheshwar (d) Harsh - Maharajadhiraja The title of Paramsaugat was held by Harshvardhan's elder brother Rajyavardhan. The history of the reign of Harshavardhan was the most illustrious Harsha of the Pushyabhuti dynasty of Thaneshwar. The history of the reign of Harshavardhana is obtained from the copper plates Rajatarangini obtained from Magadha, and from the description of the Chinese traveler Yuwancwang.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- Kumarpal was a Chalukya dynasty ruler of Gujarat. He became the king after Jai Singh. Jain texts tell us that Kumarpal attacked the ruler of Malwa, Ballal, killed him and defeated the Shilahar dynasty ruler of Konkar in the battle. He suppressed the rebellion of Parmars of Mount Abu and Virat and kept them under his control. In this way Kumarpal proved to be a great and powerful king of his era. He was a Jain follower. He preached non-violence in his kingdom and banned sacrificial violence. Following Jainism, Kumarpal had banned animal killing, horse racing and production and sale of liquor in the state. But despite being a Jain, he went to Somnath temple and worshiped Lord Shiva and also built some Shaiva temples.
(Uउण Nू.-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह, 2015) व्याख्: (Uun Nu.-घुघ्घ झाजी वल्ह, 2015) Explanation – It is mentioned in Buddhist texts that Ashoka built 84 thousand stupas. Ashoka had built the Mahastupa of Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh. Amravati Stupa was built by the rulers of Ikshvaku dynasty. Dhamekh Stupa of Sarnath was built during the Gupta period. It is made of bricks. Gupta ruler Kumaragupta had built Nalanda University. 284
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2003 254: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2003 254 Explanation- The author of Katha Manjari (Vhritkatha Manjari) is Kshemendra. In order to make this stanza elegant, the poet has included some other stories in the original story. The basic objective of this work is to introduce the scholars of culture to the stories of the great story. There are many characteristics in Kshemendra's narrative system. Kshemendra found skill in describing the female beauty and bravery of the princess. It has a total of 7500 verses which are divided into 16 pambakas (sagax). At times the language has become clear and comprehensible. The description of tra+tuas and natural phenomena is also full of miracles. Kshemendra has beautifully included Hasyaras in the story. Through this he ridiculed the hypocrites of his era. The purpose of Kshemendra's creation was not only to present interesting and funny stories but also to improve the life of common people through moral principles.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2006 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2006 Explanation: Manikyakvachagar was born in a Brahmin family of a village near Madura. He defeated the Buddhists of Lanka in a debate at Chidambaram. He wrote many devotional songs, which have been collected in Thiruvachakam. Manikyakavachakar Nayanar was a Shaiva saint. The number of Nayanar Shaiva saints is said to be 63, in which apart from Manikyakavachakar, the names of Appar, Tirugnana, Sambandra, Sundramuth etc. are notable. His devotional songs have been compiled together in 'Devaram'.
Uउण NET-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–: Uun NET-घुघ्घ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – Stabo was a Greek geographer and historian. He was born in Amasia, Asia Minor, about 63 years before Christ. The classical (or Roman) writer Stabo had said, 'Mostly those who have written about India are a tribe of liars - Demachus is first in that list, Megasthenes is second, while Aenecritus and Niax, likewise others, stammer out a few (correct) words.
Uउण NET-घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–क्: Uun NET-घुझ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – Kulottunga I (1070-1120 AD) was the son of Eastern Chalukya king Rajaraja but there was a mixture of Chola Ratta in him. His mother was the daughter of Rajendra Chola. He himself was married to the daughter of Rajendra II, the winner of the Koppam battle. Kulottung consolidated his position by suppressing his rebels. He proved to be a powerful ruler of his time. Meanwhile, Sinhala king Vijay Bahu declared his independence against Kulotung. He anointed himself in 1072-73 AD and Kulottung had to accept his independence. Over time, there was a rapprochement between the two and Kulottung married his daughter to a Sinhala prince.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2001 Explanation- Viharaja IV (1153-1162) was the most powerful ruler among the Chauhanvanshi kings. He captured Delhi by defeating the Tomar kings. Information about this victory comes from the Bijolia article. The struggle of the Chauhan rulers against the Tomar rulers of Delhi had been going on for a long time but till now they had not achieved success. Ending the independence of the Tomar dynasty and making it his vassal was Viharaj's biggest success. According to Dasharatha Sharma, the defeated Tomar king was Tanwar. Viharaja also got success against his contemporary Chalukya and Paramara kings. His father Anaxraj had to be defeated at the hands of Chalukya ruler Kumar Pal. Therefore, with the aim of washing away this stigma, Viharaja started a war against the Chalukyas. He defeated Kumarpal and took control of Mewar and Marwar.
Uउण NET-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी व्aह. 2017 व्याख्या–: Uun NET-घघ्घ झजाजी वाह. 2017 Explanation – Pallava king Mahendravarman (600-630 AD), who was also known as 'weird-minded', was among the greatest rulers of the Pallava dynasty. He had assumed the titles of Matavilas, Vichitrachitra, Gunbhar etc. He was a great producer, poet and musician. Hence statement (A) is wrong. Mahendravarman, under the influence of Shaiva saint Appar, abandoned Jainism and accepted Shaivism. He built many cave temples and composed 'Mattavilasprahasana'.

Firoz was the first Sultan who gave priority to the material well-being of his subjects over conquests and wars, and expanded the duties of the ruler. He made Islam the basis of state governance. Assistance to the unemployed, establishment of Diwan-e-Khairat and charitable (Darul-Shap) hospital were his humanitarian works. Firoz introduced vocational curriculum in education.

Balban adopted a policy of 'iron and blood' towards his opponents. The famous Persian poets of this time were Amir Khusro and Amir Hasan. Tughril's rebellion in Bengal took place during this time.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000, 200: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000, 2001 Explanation – Iltutmish was the first Turkish ruler who introduced pure Arabic coins. Its contribution to the monetary system is the highest. Because he introduced two major silver coins i.e. silver tanka and copper jital. Iltutmish got the name of the Caliph inscribed on the coins. He also declared himself the 'chief protector of religion' Nasir-Amir-ul-Mumnin. Large silver coins with these names inscribed on them were introduced for the first time by 'Iltutmish'. Iltutmish can also be given the credit for popularizing the tradition of writing the name of the mint on the coins prevalent in foreign countries in India. The credit for popularizing Jital as a distinct coin also goes to Iltumish.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2007 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2007 Explanation - After the death of Bahlol Lodi, his third son Nizam Khan ascended the throne of Lodi dynasty by the name of Sikandar Lodi. He was the son of a Hindu woman, hence some nobles of the court opposed his ascension. But ignoring these opposition, he ascended the throne of Delhi in 1489 AD. He did many important works during his rule, including developing a new scale, Gaje Sikandri, for determining land revenue. Since he was an educated person, he had interest in literary works. For this purpose he established a translation department. On his own orders, he got a chapter of Ayurveda translated by the name 'Tibet-e-Sikandri'. He abolished the tax on food grains. But he reversed his father's principle of kingship and adopted Tuka and Hindu principles in place of Afghan ideals.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2011 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2011 Explanation – After dealing with Prithviraj, Paramdev Dev had to face the fierce attack of TukaX from which he could not escape. In 1203 AD, Qutbuddin defeated Paramdev and captured the fort of Kalajar. Paramadidev died in the fort of Kaeljar itself.
फ्ग्ुपी Edल. Exaस. (शd. History्) 2013 व: FGP Edel. Exas. (Shd. History) 2013 Explanation- As soon as his power over the country became stronger, Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316 AD) oppressed the rich. The Sultan ordered that all the landed property, villages and other lands held by the people in the form of milk (property), inam and wakyap (gifts) should be taken back and converted into Khalsa land.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घुघगाह History अज्ञ., 2004 UPPCS (झुर) घुघगाह History, 2003 Explanation- Ushri land (Ushr) was the land tax taken from Muslims and this land was irrigated by natural means from which 10³ part of the crop was taken as land tax. Piroz Shah Tughlaq imposed only four taxes accepted by Islamic laws, Kharaj (levy), Khums (1/5 of the wealth looted in war), Jizya (religious tax on Hindus) and Zakat (21/2 percent of the income), which were taken from Muslims and spent for their welfare. Piroz Tughlaq also imposed irrigation tax after the approval of the Ulema class. Those farmers who used water from the royal canals for irrigation. He had to give 1/10th of his produce to the government. Apart from these taxes, all other taxes were removed. Ordered government employees not to demand more than the appropriate tax. Probably in his time the rent was 1/5 to 1/3 of the crop. His main function was to settle the revenue of the entire nation on an estimated basis so that the income of the state was fixed.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2001 व्या: UPPCS (Jr) Ghhgah History, 2001 Explanation- Qutbuddin Aibak, the ruler of the Ghulam dynasty, had established the capital of Delhi Sultanate at Lahir. His successor Iltutmish, who is called the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate, first shifted the capital from Lahir to Delhi. Iltutmish completed the works which Aybak had left incomplete. By eliminating the Aldaiz and Kucha, he freed the Delhi Sultanate from its claim to the ownership of Gor and Ghazni. He proved the reality of the Delhi Sultanate by recapturing the territories snatched away by the Rajput rulers of Rajasthan and by suppressing the rebellion of Deab. By protecting the Delhi Sultanate from the Mongol invasion, he saved it from great trouble. Dr. K. M. Nizami has written - Aybak had made a mental outline about the outline of the Delhi Sultanate. Iltutmish gave him a personality, a position, a driving force, a direction, a governance system and a ruling class.
Uउण NET-घ्घ झ्aजी व्aह. 2017 व्याख्या–सु: Uun NET-घघ झाजी वाह. 2017 Explanation – Ibn Battuta has written the above description while mentioning the feasts organized by Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq (1325-1351 AD) for his nobles and foreign guests. Ibn Battuta was a resident of Africa and came to India as a traveler in 1333 AD. Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq appointed him to the post of Qazi of Delhi in 1334 AD. Ibn Battuta was sent by Mubin Tughlaq as his ambassador to China in 1342. In which post he worked for ten years. Ibn Battuta has given a detailed description of the circumstances of the reign of Sultan Muhammad Tughlaq in his book Rehla.
फ्ग्ुपी Edल. Exaस. (शd. History्) 2013 व: FGP Edel. Exas. (शद. History) 2013 Explanation- Balban (1265-1287 AD) ruled Delhi for 20 years as Wazir and for 20 years as Sultan. He adopted the 'policy of blood and iron' to establish the prestige of the post of Sultan. According to him, the Sultan is his own representative on earth and his position is only after the Prophet. Balban also propounded the principle of 'Niyabat-e-Khudai' (representative of God).

In 1309 AD he sent Malik Kafur to complete this task. Warangal, the capital of the Kakatiya kingdom, was surrounded by strong walls. The attack was carried out immediately. Kafur surrounded Warangal and caused huge damage to the defense forces inside. So the king surrendered. 300 elephants, 7000 horses and a large amount of cash and gems were presented to the invader to compensate for the war damage and promised to pay heavy tribute. 345
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History एजट., 2008 Explanation – Nasiruddin Khusro – He was an Indian Muslim. Initially he was a Gujarati Hindu of a low caste called Bharwar or Gadriya, later he accepted Islam. He was the Sultan of Delhi from 15 April to 5 September 1320. Ghiyasuin Tughlaq - He was born in a low caste. His father was a slave of Balban and his mother was a Jatni of Punjab. He ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1320-1325 AD. Firoz Tughlaq - Firoz was born in 1309. He was the son of Rajab, younger brother of Ghiyasuin Tughlaq. His mother was the daughter of Bhattar Rajput king Samal of Abohar, located in Hisar district of modern-day eastern Punjab. His reign was from 1351 to 1388 AD. Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517 AD) – He was the son of a goldsmith mother.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2009 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2009 Explanation─Balban made good arrangements for the defense of Tuka Sultanate and gave it a new life, this was his most important work. He was a person with strong willpower. He re-established internal peace and made proper arrangements to protect the north-western borders of the Sultanate and saved it from Mongol attacks. He did not try to conquer the lands of neighboring Hindu rulers. Due to his strong will power and harsh nature, he crushed the power of big Tuk feudal lords and gave a new shape to the Tuk rule in this country. Hence, he was not a weak-willed person.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 Explanation- On the basis of available facts, it seems that there was widespread corruption during the rule of Pirojshah. According to Apeep, Sultan's Wazir Khan-e-Jahan Maqbool himself was famous for honesty but even such a Wazir was unable to stop corruption. Almost all the Apsars were bribe takers. Imad-ul-Mulk Vashir Multani had accumulated immense wealth through corrupt means. The same wealth became the cause of fights and conspiracies among his ten brothers after the death of Pirojshah. The misuse of government positions increased so much that the rich used to re-impose those taxes which were abolished on the grounds that they were considered un-Islamic. Apip mentions a horseman to whom the Sultan gave a tanka from his treasury so that he could bribe him to get his horses passed in the court.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2009 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2009 Explanation─Rukunu was the eldest surviving son of Firoz Iltutmish, his mother's name was Shahtukan while Razia was the eldest daughter who ruled from 1236-1240 AD. Muizzuddin Bahram was the third son of Shah Iltutmish who ruled from 1240-1242 AD after the fall of Razia. Nasiruddin Mahmood, who sat on the throne on June 10, 1246 AD after the fall of Alauddin Masoodshah, was not the child but the grandson of Iltutmish, who ruled in a simple manner till 1265 AD. Who was the last successor of Iltutmish's dynasty. After that Balban succeeded Eshahsan who ruled till 1287 AD.

: क्ुतुबुöीन एेबक (1206 - 1210) भारत में: Qutubuddin Aibak (1206 - 1210) was the founder of the Tuka Empire in India. He was a slave who was bought by Mohammad Ghori. Due to his ability, skill and leadership, after the second battle of Tarain in 1192 AD, he was appointed the ruler of the Indian Empire by Mohammad Ghori. Scholars like Hasan Nizami and Fakr-e-Mudaibbar found shelter in his court. Built a mosque named 'Quwwat-ul-Islam' in Delhi and 'Dhai Din Ka Jhopad' in Ajmer. Muslim writers called him 'Lakhbakhsh' because of his generosity. And because of reading the Quran in a melodious voice, he was called 'Quran Khan'. Minhaj-us-Siraj, the author of Tabaqate Nasiri, called Aibak 'Hatim II'. Started the construction of Qutub Minar in Delhi, but it was completed by Iltutmish.

UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2007 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2007 Explanation-Many important constructions were made in the field of architecture during the Lodi period. A large number of tombs were built during this period, most of which were built on the lines of Khane Jahan Telangani tombs. It is noteworthy that the tomb of Khane Jahan Telangani is a beautiful example of an octagonal tomb. However, during the time of Sikandar Lodi, a new trend started in the field of architecture in which the construction of two domes started instead of one dome. Pasa Baun has addressed the period of Syed and Lodi as the era of tombs.
