Firishta writes that Humayun was unique in astrology and mathematics. He used to write very beautiful poems. Humayun's library was full of books from India and abroad. Apart from this, he also used to take some books with him during military campaigns.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2011 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2011 Explanation – During the reign of Jahangir, the British also tried to get trade facilities from the emperor and William Hawkins and Sir Thomas Roe met the emperor as representatives of Britain. Jahangir had given a mansab of 400 to Hawkins. Apart from this, he also got opposition from English Khan or Firangi Khan.
आश्रम पद्धति Lect. Exam. 2009 G.I.C. Lec: Ashram Method Lect. Exam. 2009 G.I.C. Lect. exam 2009
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह. 2015) व्याख: (Uun Nu.- घघघ झजाजी वल्ह. 2015) Explanation – Sher Shah did many works for the welfare of the people. Apart from this, he generously made arrangements for the livelihood of the blind, the elderly, handicapped, widows and scholars. Contemporary historian Abbas Khan Serwani writes that he had arranged langar (free food) in his army for destitutes, beggars and destitutes. They were given very tasty food.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 Explanation- After the end of the Southern War in 1621 AD, due to the rebellion of Shahjahan and Mahvat Khan, the Mughals could not get the opportunity to pay attention towards the south during the time of Jahangir. In fact, due to the expansion of the border, the Mughals did not achieve any special success during the time of Jahangir, but there is no doubt that the pressure of the Mughals on the southern states increased. On the occasion of Shahjahan's rebellion, Malik Ambar once again opposed the Mughal emperor with the help of Shahjahan. It was clear that the Ahmednagar state was not yet ready to accept Mughal power. Malik Ambar died in 1626 AD. But the situation of the Mughals in the south remained almost the same as before. Till that time Ahmednagar, Bijapur and Golkund were not under the control of the Mughals. In such a situation, Jahangir died in 1627 AD.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गह हिस्ट्य एज्ट., 2004 Explanation- Peter Mundy - 1628- during the time of Shahjahan, Ralph Pitch - 1585 during the time of Akbar, William Hawkins- 1608 during the time of Jahangir, Sir Thomas Roe- 1615 during the time of Jahangir.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ झ्aजी अम. 2012) व्याख्या –: (Uun No.- घुझ झाजी Am. 2012) Explanation – Orissa was conquered by Akbar in 1592 AD through Mana Singh. In 1573 AD, Akbar introduced the Dag system. So that Mansabadar cannot change horses and maintain the correct number of horses and riders. In 1580 AD, the entire empire was divided into 12 provinces. Reformed caste and rider in 1595 AD.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2010 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2010 Explanation – In 1653 AD, Aurangzeb was appointed the Governor of the South for the second time. During the second reign, Aurangzeb introduced the same revenue system in the south, which was introduced by Tedarmal in the north. Mushad Quli Khan helped him in this work. Farmers were given advance money to buy tools and seeds. Capable and honest persons were appointed as administrators and as a result the pace of governance improved.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2009 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2009 Explanation─In 1580-81 AD, Akbar had to face the worst difficulties of his life. He was subjected to a very difficult test. The rebellion in India, the invasion of Kabul and the discontent in the camp all together tested his endurance and ability, yet Akbar continued to fight the storm courageously and was able to overcome every difficulty, to commemorate this huge success, the Vishak Durbar of 1582 was celebrated on a large scale. All the Subedars got permission to attend. On this occasion, he started the festival of Nowruz, which was celebrated by the early Sultans of Delhi in imitation of the ancient Iranian Shahs. The work of revenue reform, which was temporarily postponed due to the dire political situation, was taken up. Tedarmal was appointed Prime Minister in 1582.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2007 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2007 Explanation – Babar, the founder of the Mughal Empire, died on 26 December 1530 AD. After his death, his body was first buried in 'Arambag' of Agra. But later, as per his wish, he was buried at a place chosen by him in Kabul.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2010 UPPC: UPPCS (झृ) घुघघाह History, 2010 UPPCS (झृ) घुघगाह History, 2002 Explanation Khwaja Abdul Samad was a painter of Humayun's time, who was honored by Humayun with the title of 'Sheeri Kalam'. This Khwaja Abdus Samad was appointed by the young emperor Akbar as the head of the royal mint and later as Diwan of Multan. Abdussamad was a painter of the Indo-Iranian (Hindu-Zaregah) style.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2005 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2005 Explanation – Ustad Mansoor was a skilled painter among the great painters of Jahangir. Mansoor had expertise in painting birds. Jahangir had honored him with the title of 'Nadir-ul-Astra'.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी अम. 2014) व्याख्या: (Uun No.- घुघ झाजी अम. 2014) Explanation – Islam Shah was a high class administrator and capable commander. He made many rules related to government administration. The policies made by Sher Shah disappeared due to his death. Akbar had adopted the land revenue system established by Sher Shah with some modifications.

(Uun No.- घुघ्घ झाजी Am. 2014) Explanation – After the death of Babar's father, Babar's maternal grandmother Isan Dailat Begum made a huge contribution in making Babar a disciplined, protected and safe person. She was virtually his advisor during his initial struggle to capture Fargana. Babur was a vulnerable boy of about 11 when Umar Sheikh Mija II died in 1494. He found himself surrounded by enemies of his own family. At that time, Isan Dailat Begum continued to stay with her grandson and guide Babar.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2010 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2010 Explanation – Shah Jahan rebelled in 1623 instead of going to Kandahar, which was completely defeated in Balochpur, south of Delhi. He kept wandering here and there. Finally in 1625 AD he was reunited with his father Jahangir. Shahjahan accepted to surrender Rohtas and Asirgarh. Aurangzeb and Dara were sent to the court as bail. Shahjahan went to Nashik with his wife Mumtaz Mahal and son Murad. 415
Aेप्araस झ्addप्aूग थम्ू. Exaस. 2009 व्य: अप्रास झड़पुग थम्ू. Exas. 2009 Explanation - Roshan Akhtar, with the help of Syed brothers, ascended the Mughal throne with the title of 'Muhammad Shah' on 28 September 1719. It was during that time that the Syed brothers came to an end and Muhammad Shah gave the post of 'Vakeel-Mutlaq' to Nizamul Mulk. During the time of Muhammad Shah, Ahmed Shah Abdali attacked India in 1748 AD.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह. 2013) व्याख्य: (Uun No.- घुझ झजाजी वल्ह. 2013) Explanation – Correct match is – (a) Second Battle of Panipat – Akbar vs Hemu (m) Battle of Haldighati – Akbar vs Maharana Pratap (m) War of Dharma – Aurangzeb vs Dara (15 April, 1658) (d) Battle of Samugarh – Aurangzeb vs Dara (29 May, 1658)
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2009 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2009 Explanation─Baj Bahadur was the ruler of Malwa, who was defeated by Akbar's commander Abdullah Khan Uzbeg in 1562 and snatched away Malwa and later Baj Bahadur was given a mansab of 400 and sent to Delhi. Zafar Khan assumed the title of Sultan Muzaffar Shah and ruled Gujarat. He died in 1411. Yusuf Adil Shah was the Sultan of Bijapur. Who established the Adilshahi dynasty, which continued till 1686 AD. Whereas the founder of Ahmed Nagar was Malik Ahmed, son of Nizamul Mulk, who established the Nizam Shahi dynasty. Shahjahan annexed it to the Mughal Empire in 1633 AD. Qutub Shah was the founder of Qutub Shahi dynasty in Golkund. Which was merged into the Mughal Empire by Aurangzeb in 1687 AD.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2008 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2008 Explanation─ Ahmednagar became a central part of the Mughal Empire during the reign of Shahjahan. The Imadshahi state of Berar was abolished by Akbar and the Nizamshahi state of Ahmednagar was abolished by Shah Jahan and incorporated into the Mughal Empire. 412
Aेप्araस झ्addप्aूग थम्ू. Exaस. 2009 व्य: अप्रास झड़पुग थम्ू. Exas. 2009 Explanation- The Mughal emperor Shahjahan was from 1627 to 1658 AD. At that time there was a golden age of architecture in India. He also laid emphasis on the development of agriculture. He had reduced the land revenue in South India due to famine and had also reduced some legitimate taxes of Kashmir due to special circumstances.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2009, 200: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2009, 2000 Explanation─The first marriage of Salim or Jahangir was with Manabai, daughter of King Bhagwan Das of Amer and sister of Mana Singh in 1585 AD. Khushro was born from this wife. Salim's second marriage was with Jagatd Gonsai (Jodhabai), daughter of Udya Singh (Marwar). From this Khurram was born. Salim had given the post of 'Shahbegum' to Manbai. In 1604 AD, Manbai committed suicide due to internal depression due to the disloyal behavior of her son Khushro. This incident affected Jahangir so much that he did not even touch food or water for four days. There were a total of 800 women in Jahangir's harem.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी अम. 2015) व्याख्या: (Uun No.- घुघ झाजी अम. 2015) Explanation – Both the assertion and the conclusion in question are correct. Mansab indicates an officer's rank, salary and size of military force. The rank or demotion of an officer was determined by the number of mansabs increased or decreased under him. 387
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह. 2015) व्याख्य: (Uun Nu.- घुझ झाजी वल्ह. 2015) Explanation – Jahangir has given the description of India in his autobiography Tuzuk-e-Jahangir. He mentioned that salt is not available in Kashmir. Hence it is imported from India.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2010 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2010 Explanation – Wazeh or Wazeh was land assigned in exchange for cash salary. The person managing it was called 'Vajhedar' whose job was to collect revenue from that land and take his salary and deposit the remaining amount in the royal treasury.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2007 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) घृघः History, 2007 Explanation-The Portuguese were the first to come to India as European traders. When Vasco-da-Gama reached Calicut with four ships on May 17, 1498, the ruler of Calicut, Zamorin welcomed him. The second expedition of Portuguese traders took place in 1500 AD, when Pedro Alvarez › Auval reached Calicut. Bathalomodias, the discoverer of Uttamasha Cape, was also with him. These trading expeditions increased the ambitions of the Portuguese. Under his new policy, he started thinking about establishing his own colony in India, as a result, Francisco de Almeide was appointed as the first Portuguese governor in 1505 AD. But the real founder of Portuguese power in India was 'Alfonso de Albuquerque' who made Cochin his headquarters.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 फ्ग्: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History, 2000 FGP Edel. Exas. (Shd. History) 2013 Explanation – In the position of prince, Aurangzeb showed himself to be a capable commander and efficient administrator. In the war of succession, he was able to achieve success against his brothers due to the dynamism, military organization, leadership and ability to make good use of the opportunity. His first military campaign was against Jujhar Singh, the ruler of Bundelkhand, in which he achieved success. After that, Aurangzeb from time to time served as the Subedar of the South (Debad), Subedar of Gujarat, the commander of the invasion of Balkh (Central Asia) and Kandahar and gained experience through military diplomacy and administration. Shahjahan had given him the title of Bahadur for his bravery and courage.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 Explanation- Babar also had less time, but due to a political and diplomatic effort, his main work started in India. The way he maintained a balance between Indian and Afghan nobles and the way he dealt with the rulers of Bihar and Bengal, he was perfect. Many Afghan chieftains joined him because of his diplomacy. Babar had also achieved success in subduing the opposing enemies. Daniel Ras has written, "The policy with which he made Sultan Ibrahim's rebellious feudal lords fight among themselves was no less than the ability of Machiavelli." But Babar did not try to organize administration, taxes, taxes and proper justice like him.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृघः History Edt., 2004 UPPCS (ःृष) वृष्ठ History, 2004, 2010 Explanation- Battle of Bahadurgarh – February, 1658 AD, Battle of Dharamt – April, 1658 AD, Samugarh War – June, 1658 AD, Devarai War – April, 1659 AD. 405
Uउण NET-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–: Uun NET-घुघ्घ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – The festival of Diwali was celebrated in the month of Katik. Houses were cleaned on this occasion. Lakshmi was worshiped on the day of Diwali. Gambling on this occasion was considered an absolute duty. People used to gamble all night long. Most of the people lost everything in this gambling. The Mughal ruler Jahangir used to take part in gambling on Diwali celebrations, which continued for three nights.
Uउण NET-घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्त्ब. 2017 381 व्या: उँ NET-घघ झाजी वल्ट्ब. 2017 381 Explanation – Francisco Pelsart (1620 – 27) was a Dutch merchant, who came to India during the Jahangir period. He was the President of the Dutch Mint at Agra. In his description, he has written about the city of Agra, its architecture as well as Noorjahan.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – Tulsidas was a contemporary of Mughal emperor Akbar. Akbar's court poet Abul Fazal has not mentioned Tulsidas in the third part of his work Akbarnama 'Aine Akbari'. Abul Fazal has listed the names of fifteen painters in his Ain-e-Akbari, who out of about a hundred painters (most of whom were Hindus) had risen to the category of excellent artists. The names of these painters are - Daswant, Vasavan, Keshav Lal, Mukand, Mishkin, Farrukh, Kalmal, Madhu Jagan, Mahesh, Khemkaran, Tara, Sawal, Hrivansh and Ram. Akbar himself took keen interest in the work of his artists. And he used to take account of the exploits every week. Used to evaluate their ability and quality and kept rewarding (or even punishing) them accordingly.
Uउण NET-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–: Uun NET-घुघ्घ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – Tajik Neelkanthi is basically a composition based on Yavana astrology, in which on the basis of Varga Kundli, the auspicious and inauspicious moment of the rainy season of the year after birth is accurately predicted and on the basis of Prashna Kundli, the upcoming auspicious and inauspicious time is accurately predicted. In this, Acharya Neelkanth has given a new dimension to Vedic astrology by coordinating the Yavana method with the principles of Vedic astrology. On the other hand, he has also done the noble work of confluence of two cultures.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ झ्aजी अम. 2013) व्याख्या─र: (Uun No. - घुझ झाजी अम. 2013) Explanation─ Indra Singh, grandson of King Jaswant Singh's elder brother Amar Singh, was given the rulership of Nagaur and the throne of Marwar by Aurangzeb on May 26, 1679, who expressed his gratitude to the king by gifting Rs 36 lakh. Similarly, when Rani Handi's kingdom was attacked by the Mughals, Rathairas and Rana Jaya Singh of Mewar supported her.
Uउण NET-घ्घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–: Uun NET-घुघ्घ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – Sher Shah also did many public welfare works. Under this, he first got roads and inns constructed. Four features are noteworthy in the roads built by him. The first road went from Lahir to Sonargaon (Bengal) which was the longest road and is called 'Sadake Azam'. He planted paldar and shade trees along these roads, so that travelers could rest under them and tie their horses.
(Uउण Nू.- घ्घ्घ झ्aजी व्ल्ह. 2014) व्याख: (Uun Nu.- घघघ झजाजी वल्ह. 2014) Explanation – Sher Shah did many public welfare works. Under this, he first constructed roads and inns. He built four roads. The first road went from Lahir to Sonargaon (Bengal), which was the longest road and was called Sadake Azam. The fourth road built by Sher Shah went from Multan to Lahir. Sher Shah did not expel Mija Hyder Deglat, the ruler of Kashmir. Sher Shah had conquered Chittor after conquering Marwar in 1544 AD. He maintained the already existing Daag and Chehra system as it was.
Aेप्araस झ्addप्aूग थम्ू. Exaस. 2009 व्य: अप्रास झड़पुग थम्ू. Exas. 2009 Explanation- Sher Shah stopped the use of old and worn out coins issued by various earlier rulers. He introduced new coins of gold, silver and copper and determined their ratio. On the coins of Sher Shah, his name, rank and name of the mint were inscribed in Arabic or Nagari script. Sher Shah's currency system was excellent which was the basis of the present British currency system.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2004 408: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2004 408 Explanation- When Vascodi-Gama landed at Calicut in 1498 AD, the colony of Arab traders settled there adopted an attitude of hostility towards them but the Zamorin welcomed the Portuguese and ordered them to take black pepper and herbs etc. The goods brought by Vasco da Gama in Portugal were sold at sixty times more than the expenses of the entire expedition. The main objective of the Portuguese in the sixteenth century was to enrich their country and their income through the use of military force. Their goal was to establish control over the spices sent to Europe and to control other Asian trade and collect taxes from it. The rulers of Portugal were determined to create a royal monopoly on eastern trade, in which there would be no interference not only from competing countries in Europe and Asia but also from private Portuguese traders.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2009 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2009 Explanation─ Edward Terry was the priest of Sir Thomas Roe. He lived in India from 1616 to 1619 AD. He has written in his travelogue that no matter where the Padshah was located, Ganga water was arranged for him. Separate employees were appointed to bring Ganga water, Ganga water was brought in beautiful copper vessels. The copper pots had galvanized handles inside and after filling with water, they were sealed tightly before giving them to the water carriers. 413
Uउण NET-घ्घ झ्aजी Nद्न. 2017 व्याख्या–भा: Uun NET-घुझ झाजी नदन. 2017 Explanation – India's ruler Akbar and Uzbekistan's ruler Abdullah Khan Uzbekistan agreed to conquer the routes leading to the holy areas of Mecca and Medina. Akbar is counted as a great emperor among the medieval rulers of the world. He was not only the best among the Mughal emperors, but he also holds the leading position among the prominent and great rulers of India.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History Astt., 2008 Explanation - Jahandarshah's second son Ajijuin assumed the title of 'Alamgir II' after becoming the king. Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk made him sit on the king's throne in place of Ahmed Shah. His reign period was from 1754 AD to 1759 AD. His entire life was spent in jail, hence he had neither experience of war nor of administration. He was fond of reading history books. During his short reign of 5 years, he remained a toy in the hands of his minister Imad-ul-Mulk.
Uउण NET-घ्घ झ्aजी व्aह. 2017 व्याख्या–ह्: Uun NET-घघ झाजी वाह. 2017 Explanation – Hameed Bano Begum gave land from her jagir for grazing of cows. Akbar was born to King Veersal of Amarkot in 1542 AD from the womb of Hmid Bano Begum. Hamid Bano was a woman of very slow nature.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2009 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2009 Explanation─After the death of Rafi-ud-Aula, the Syed brothers installed Roshan Akhtar on the Mughal throne in the name of Muhammad Shah. This was the fourth son of Bahadur Shah I. It is said about this that never before had a more careless emperor sat on the throne of Delhi. Muhammad Shah was a young boy of 17 years, who spent most of his time within the walls of the palace with the eunuchs and women of the harem. No one had paid attention to his education because no one had even thought that he would sit on the throne of Delhi. Due to his indifference towards public affairs and his engrossment in music, he was called 'Muhammad Shah Rangeela'.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2003 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2003 Explanation- 'Akbarnama' is a famous work of Abul Pazal. After seven years of hard work, Abul Pazal completed the Akbarnama and presented it to Akbar in 1597-98. It is divided into three volumes. The third volume is 'Ain-e-Akbari'. 'Ain-e-Akbari' is the life of Akbar Nama. It has five parts. There are 10 ain's in the first part, 30 in the second and 16 ain's in the third and in the fourth part there is mention of the castes, tra+tuas, ribs and natural beauty of India. The subjects like politics, literature, religious life of Hindus and their judicial system etc. have been highlighted in detail. At the end, biographies of Indian saints and some foreign saints are given. The fifth part contains only two chapters, which contain Akbar's sayings and Abul Pajal's autobiography. Aine Akbari gives a detailed description of Akbar's administrative system.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2005 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2005 Explanation – Tobacco was brought to India by the Portuguese in 1605 AD. Probably around this time, tobacco was brought to India from America. Tobacco cultivation was started during the time of Jahangir, after some time Emperor Jahangir banned the cultivation of tobacco.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गह हिस्ट्य अज्ञ., 2004 Explanation- Babar (1526-30 AD), who established the Mughal Empire in India by defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the first battle of Panipat in 1526 AD, had warned his son Humayun by calling the Afghan leader Sher Khan a cunning Afghan. In fact, this assessment of Babar turned out to be absolutely true and Sher Khan (Sher Shah Suri) defeated Humayun in the battle of Chausa (1539 AD) and Kannauj or Bilgram (1540 AD) and took over the power of Delhi and Humayun was forced to go into exile.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- Babar was the founder of the Mughal Empire. In November 1525, Babar left Kabul with the aim of conquering India. Babar moved towards Delhi. Ibrahim Lodi moved towards Punjab to confront him and both their armies faced each other in the plains of Panipat. On 21 April 1526, the war started in the morning and its decision was taken by afternoon. Babar won the war, Ibrahim Lodi was killed and the Afghan army was destroyed. Babar's artillery, his war strategy, mainly the use of Tulgama war strategy, and his commander's ability were the main reasons for his victory. The battle of Panipat decided not only the fate of India but definitely the fate of the Lodi dynasty. After winning the battle of Panipat, Babar gave one siqiqa dan each to the people of Kabul. Babar is addressed with the title of 'Kalandra'.
Aेप्araस झ्addप्aूग थम्ू. Exaस. 2012 व्य: अप्रास झड़पुग थम्ू. Exas. 2012 Explanation – After the death of Akbar II in 1837 AD, his son Bahadur Shah became the second Mughal emperor. After the rebellion of 1857, the Anjas removed Bahadur Shah (a) from Goi and exiled him to Raghun, where he died after a few days. Even today his tomb is situated in Rangoon.
उ.घ.ण. थम्ू. Exaस 2009, 2015 UPPCS (झ्r): U.G.H. Thummu. Exas 2009, 2015 UPPCS (झृ) घुघगाह History Ext., 2008 UPPCS (झृ) घुगाह History 2000 Explanation- Jahangir became the Mughal emperor in 1605 AD. His childhood name was Salim. His first marriage was with Manbai, daughter of Raja Bhagwandas of Amber (Jaipur) in 1585 AD. Khusro was the son of this Manbai. There was a difference of opinion between Jahangir and his son Khusrao over becoming the emperor, due to this conflict, Manbai committed suicide by consuming opium, whose tomb is located in Khusrobagh, Allahabad. Jahangir had given the title of 'Shahbegum' to this Manbai.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2000 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2000 Explanation – Jahangir's wife Mehrunisan Begum was Muslim and everyone else was Rajput. Mehrunisan's father Giyasbeg was a resident of Pasiya. After the death of his father Khwaja Muhammad Sharif, Mija Ghiyasbeg left for India with his two sons and daughter with the intention of trying his luck elsewhere. On the way, near Kandahar, his wife gave birth to another girl and this girl was Mehruninsa. Mija Giyasbeg got a place in Akbar's service and he progressed with his ability. Jahangir gave him the title of 'Atmaduula' in his early days. In 1594 AD, Mehruninsa was married to Alikuli Beg. After the death of Alikuli Beg, Mehruninsa was appointed the maid of Akbar's widow Salima Begum. 1611 AD Jahangir saw her during the festival of Nowruz and fell in love with her. May, 1611 AD Jahangir married her and gave her the titles of 'Noormahal' and Noorjahan.

He propounded coherent philosophical principles which are known as 'Vishishtadvaitavad'. Madhvacharya was born in 1199 AD. He was a great leader of the Bhatti movement of the South. He believed in 'dualism' and considered both soul and God as separate. He was mainly a worshiper of 'Lakshmi Narayan'. Nimbak was another important saint who lived in the 12th century. He was a worshiper of Radha-Krishna. His opinion is known as 'Dvaitadvaitavaad'. Their sect is also known as 'Sanak sect'. Vallabhacharya was born in Varanasi in 1479 AD. He belonged to a Brahmin family of Telangana and believed in Krishna Bhatti. His belief is known as 'Shuddhavaitavaad'. On the basis of the above mentioned facts, the answer to the question – Ramanuja – Vishishtadvaita; Madhvacharya-Dualism; nimbak-dvaitadvaita; Vallabhacharya - Shuddhadvaita Hega.
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History् एज्त., 200: UPPCS (झृ) घृह्गाह History Ejt., 2008 Explanation – Wazir or Diwan was an important official of the Mughal Empire. Divided it into parts. First, Wazir-e-Tapveez, second Wazir-e-Tanpeez. Wazir-e-Tapweez was a minister with unlimited powers. He was considered the ruler's household manager and close friend. Sometimes he appointed officers without the prior permission of the emperor and later informed the emperor about it. The Wazir-e-Tanpij was an officer with limited authority. Mirbakshi was the head of the military department during the Mughal period. Khanesama was the head of the royal kitchen (home department).
UPPCS (झ्r) घ्ह्ग्aह History्, 2002 व्या: UPPCS (झृ) Ghhgah History, 2002 Explanation- Urdu literature developed during the Mughal period. The subsequent Mughal ruler Muhammad Shah (1719-48 AD) provided royal patronage to Urdu. He invited Shamshuddin Wali to his court and encouraged him for the development of Urdu. According to the famous author William Arvin, there were many parties in the Mughal court. The four main ones were Turani, Irani, Apaghani and Hindustani. Three of these Central Asians were descendants of Iranian and Afghan soldiers who had conquered India and helped establish kingdoms here. Their number increased greatly in the last 25 years of Aurangzeb's reign, especially when he was busy in the wars in the south. Their descendants were appointed on military and civilian posts in different parts of India.

In Sirhind, Mughal officers were removed and Sikh officers were appointed and there was a continuous conflict with the Mughals. Their big commanders were in collusion with the Anjos, used to send them information, and did not fight at the right time. On December 31, 1845, the Sikh army had crossed the Sutlej river and probably its objective was to suddenly attack Firozpur, but this objective could not be fulfilled due to the betrayal of Lal Singh. Lal Singh had written to Nicholson, the British representative in Firozpur – I have crossed the Sutlej with the Sikh army. You know my friendship with eggs, tell me what should I do now. Nicholson replied, "Do not attack Firozpur, spend as many days as possible and then move towards the Governor General." Lal Singh did the same and Firozpur was saved.
